groups.subject_en: The player's white pawn, the hero of the game: the weakest chess piece, left alone on the rug after the war. A small ivory Staunton pawn (round head ball, flat collar ring, smooth tapering body, flared round base) that is scuffed and mended: a faded blue-grey cloth tie around the collar with two tiny stitch marks, a worn base rim. Two small dark dot eyes and no mouth (the pawn is silent; feeling is shown only by eye shape and posture). No arms, no legs, never royal: no crown, no cross. Its weapons (toy sword, pencil spear, ruler blade, eraser) are separate overlay sprites on a weapon pivot and are NEVER drawn on the body; keep the front edge of the piece clear for them. The body, outline included, fits an 18x22 px box inside the 32x32 canvas, which is exactly one cell: the pawn is smaller than its cell, a little slimmer and lower than the placeholder pawn the generator draws today, which fills the whole cell width, so that it keeps at least 2 px of empty canvas on every side.
groups.details_en: Squash and stretch is done by compressing or elongating the whole piece by whole pixels (1-2 px), never by blurring. Anticipation frames are visibly longer in feel than impact frames; the impact frame is the single brightest frame. Tone is serious and tender: no cartoon grin, no sweat drops, no stars, no hearts. These are the three still facing bodies shown when no clip is playing and used as the first frame reference for every clip. The west facing is the east image mirrored by the tools. CELL FIT (owner decision 2026-10-12: a chess piece is smaller than its cell). The canvas is 32x32, exactly one cell. The standing pawn body is at most 18x22 px, outline included, centred on x=16 with its base rim on y=30, so its top sits at y=8 and at least 2 px of empty canvas remain on every side: never exactly cell-sized, never taller than the cell, never touching or crossing a canvas edge. Relative heights follow a real chess set (pawn 22 px, knight, bishop and rook 24, queen 26, king 28; bosses on one cell are a little wider than their class and never beyond 24x28). In EVERY frame, squash, stretch, tilt, lean, lunge and lift included, every pixel of the piece stays inside x 2..29 and y 2..29: the headroom above the resting top is 6 px, a lift and a stretch together never use more than that, and a tilt or lean never pushes a side past x=2 or x=29; if a pose would not fit, shorten the stretch or the lift first and never the margin. The pixel measures written in the poses are already scaled to this body size.
groups.avoid_en: arms, hands, legs, weapons drawn on the body, a crown, a face with mouth, gore, blood, cartoon sweat or stars, motion-blur smears, outline colour changes between frames, pure white or pure black fills, any background or floor shadow
groups.palette_en: Flash frames lighten every body pixel toward white for exactly one frame; the pawn is never red.
groups.notes_vi: Ba ảnh tĩnh của pawn khi đứng yên: nhìn thẳng (body.png), nhìn lên (body_n), nhìn phải (body_e). Hướng trái tool tự lật từ hướng phải.

groups.notes_vi: Chỉ vẽ thân pawn lao tới; kiếm, bút chì và vệt chém là sprite riêng. Đâm bút chì phải dài và nặng hơn chém kiếm. groups.title_vi: Pawn: Rule Step (nhảy chữ L) và Free Step (bước chéo)
groups.anchor: base-bottom centre at (16,30): the base rim sits on the line y=30 (the lowest drawn body row is y=29) with 2 px of empty canvas under it; every chess piece stands on this one anchor, so a shorter piece just leaves more empty canvas above its head; in flight frames the base is drawn up to 4 px higher on the canvas but its centre column stays at x=16 and the whole piece stays inside the 2 px margin
groups.subject_en: The player's white pawn, the hero of the game: the weakest chess piece, left alone on the rug after the war. A small ivory Staunton pawn (round head ball, flat collar ring, smooth tapering body, flared round base) that is scuffed and mended: a faded blue-grey cloth tie around the collar with two tiny stitch marks, a worn base rim. Two small dark dot eyes and no mouth (the pawn is silent; feeling is shown only by eye shape and posture). No arms, no legs, never royal: no crown, no cross. Its weapons (toy sword, pencil spear, ruler blade, eraser) are separate overlay sprites on a weapon pivot and are NEVER drawn on the body; keep the front edge of the piece clear for them. The body, outline included, fits an 18x22 px box inside the 32x32 canvas, which is exactly one cell: the pawn is smaller than its cell, a little slimmer and lower than the placeholder pawn the generator draws today, which fills the whole cell width, so that it keeps at least 2 px of empty canvas on every side.
groups.details_en: Squash and stretch is done by compressing or elongating the whole piece by whole pixels (1-2 px), never by blurring. Anticipation frames are visibly longer in feel than impact frames; the impact frame is the single brightest frame. Tone is serious and tender: no cartoon grin, no sweat drops, no stars, no hearts. Rule Step is the Knight's L-leap borrowed by the pawn (takeoff 0.08 s, flight 0.22 s untargetable, landing recovery 0.25 s); it passes over obstacles, so flight frames sit visibly above the floor. Free Step is the pawn's first-ever diagonal step, the climax of the game: it must feel rare and dramatic but still be a one-cell step (0.18 s). Directional clips are drawn for south, north and east for the L-leap and for south-east and north-east for the diagonal; the other facings are tool mirrors. CELL FIT (owner decision 2026-10-12: a chess piece is smaller than its cell). The canvas is 32x32, exactly one cell. The standing pawn body is at most 18x22 px, outline included, centred on x=16 with its base rim on y=30, so its top sits at y=8 and at least 2 px of empty canvas remain on every side: never exactly cell-sized, never taller than the cell, never touching or crossing a canvas edge. Relative heights follow a real chess set (pawn 22 px, knight, bishop and rook 24, queen 26, king 28; bosses on one cell are a little wider than their class and never beyond 24x28). In EVERY frame, squash, stretch, tilt, lean, lunge and lift included, every pixel of the piece stays inside x 2..29 and y 2..29: the headroom above the resting top is 6 px, a lift and a stretch together never use more than that, and a tilt or lean never pushes a side past x=2 or x=29; if a pose would not fit, shorten the stretch or the lift first and never the margin. The pixel measures written in the poses are already scaled to this body size. In flight frames the art lifts the base by at most 4 px (the rest of the jump arc is the engine's, and the separate flight shadow shows the height).
groups.avoid_en: arms, hands, legs, weapons drawn on the body, a crown, a face with mouth, gore, blood, cartoon sweat or stars, motion-blur smears, outline colour changes between frames, pure white or pure black fills, any background or floor shadow, spinning or tumbling, wings, trails longer than 2 px
groups.palette_en: Flash frames lighten every body pixel toward white for exactly one frame; the pawn is never red. The flight rim light is pale white, not blue (blue is the child's colour).
groups.notes_vi: Rule Step là bước nhảy chữ L của Mã, pawn mượn dùng. Free Step là bước chéo đầu tiên trong game nên phải 'hiếm' và đẹp. Chỉ vẽ se và ne cho Free Step.

The standing pawn body is at most 18x22 px, outline included, centred on x=16 with its base rim on y=30, so its top sits at y=8 and at least 2 px of empty canvas remain on every side: never exactly cell-sized, never taller than the cell, never touching or crossing a canvas edge. Relative heights follow a real chess set (pawn 22 px, knight, bishop and rook 24, queen 26, king 28; bosses on one cell are a little wider than their class and never beyond 24x28). In EVERY frame, squash, stretch, tilt, lean, lunge and lift included, every pixel of the piece stays inside x 2..29 and y 2..29: the headroom above the resting top is 6 px, a lift and a stretch together never use more than that, and a tilt or lean never pushes a side past x=2 or x=29; if a pose would not fit, shorten the stretch or the lift first and never the margin. poses_en: Lying flat on its side on the floor, base pointing away from the camera, head ball resting on the rug, eyes closed as two short horizontal lines, perfectly still: the exact pose of the fallen pieces in room T1. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Still on its side; a tiny twitch: the base lifts 1 px, one eye opens as a thin dark slit, the cloth tie slightly shifted. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Rocking: the body rolls 20 degrees toward upright pivoting on the base rim, both eyes half open, the head ball lifting off the floor. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Shoving up: the body is 45 degrees from vertical with the base planted, stretched 2 px taller, eyes wide and startled. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Overshoot wobble: past upright and tilted 10 degrees the other way, squash 1 px then stretch 1 px, eyes small and relieved. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Settled fully upright, eyes open looking forward, base flat on the floor, the plain upright standing pose. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Lean down: the body tilts forward 20 degrees toward the item cell in front, the head ball lowered, eyes on the item. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Reach: a deeper tilt of 30 degrees with the base planted, eyes locked on the item. The item itself is NOT drawn. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Rise with delight: the body springs upright stretched 2 px, a tiny 2 px hop, eyes bright. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Settle: lands with a small squash and a glad small tilt of the head ball. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.

Impact: the body squashes sideways 2 px wider and 2 px shorter, eyes squeezed into tight > < marks, every body pixel lightened toward white for this one frame. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Recoil: the body tilts 15 degrees backward, the base slides 2 px back, eyes still squeezed, the pale-blue shadow band deepened. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Wobble back: the tilt reduces to 5 degrees, eyes open wide in shock, ready to return to idle. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Stagger: the body tilts 12 degrees, eyes squeezed shut, one side of the base rim lifting. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Tipping: tilt 30 degrees, the base lifted 2 px on the far side, eyes as small dizzy dots, the tie flaring. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Falling: tilt 60 degrees, the head ball dropping, eyes closed. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Floor impact: the piece lies on its side with a 2 px bounce and a squash on contact. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Settling: it rolls 10 degrees back and forth once on its curved body, the last motion. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.

Lying on its side motionless, eyes closed as short lines: exactly the same lying pose as the start of the wake clip (on its side, base pointing away from the camera, head ball resting on the rug). Toy-like, gentle, no gore. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Crouch: the body squashes 2 px, eyes closed in one deep calm breath. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Spring: the body stretches 2 px and rises 2 px off the floor. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Peak: the base is 4 px up, the body upright and the head ball tilted back slightly, eyes bright. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Land: squash 2 px with a small flourish, the tie swinging forward. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Stand tall: stretched 1 px taller than rest, head ball lifted slightly, calm proud eyes. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Hold: the steady resolve pose, upright and calm, eyes looking forward, safe to loop on. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.

groups.subject_en: The player's white pawn, the hero of the game: the weakest chess piece, left alone on the rug after the war. Two small dark dot eyes and no mouth (the pawn is silent; feeling is shown only by eye shape and posture). No arms, no legs, never royal: no crown, no cross. Its weapons (toy sword, pencil spear, ruler blade, eraser) are separate overlay sprites on a weapon pivot and are NEVER drawn on the body; keep the front edge of the piece clear for them. The body, outline included, fits an 18x22 px box inside the 32x32 canvas, which is exactly one cell: the pawn is smaller than its cell, a little slimmer and lower than the placeholder pawn the generator draws today, which fills the whole cell width, so that it keeps at least 2 px of empty canvas on every side.
groups.details_en: Squash and stretch is done by compressing or elongating the whole piece by whole pixels (1-2 px), never by blurring. Anticipation frames are visibly longer in feel than impact frames; the impact frame is the single brightest frame. Tone is serious and tender: no cartoon grin, no sweat drops, no stars, no hearts. The pawn is silent; these clips are its whole voice in cutscenes. 'bow' is for the fallen King (E in T1) and for the child's hand; 'hesitate' plays when the hand first arrives; 'head_shake' is the denial when the player presses a diagonal chord before Free Step exists (T1 onward, again at the Queen's seal); 'rescue_hold' loops while the player holds E to free a trapped piece; 'direction_restored' plays in the three Act-6 memory alcoves. the two held stills (the pawn lifted by its base and hanging straight, and the same pose tilted 15 degrees) are the images the engine places at the contact point of the child's hand while that hand picks the pawn up and sets it down (the hand is a separate set of files); the toppled pawn those clips lift is the pawn lying flat on its side, exactly as in the last frame of its own defeat animation. groups.notes_vi: Pawn không nói, các clip này là toàn bộ giọng nói của nó. Lắc đầu chỉ xoay quả cầu đầu, thân đứng yên. poses_en: Upright: a respectful start pose, eyes open and quiet. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Bowing: the body tilts forward 20 degrees, the head ball lowering. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Deepest bow, held: tilt 35 degrees, the head ball lowest, eyes closed as short lines. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Rise: the body returns upright, eyes open, a quiet 1 px sag of grief. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Looks up: the head ball tilts back 15 degrees and the eyes glance up toward something very large overhead; the body is still. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Shrinks back: the base slides 2 px back, the body leans back 10 degrees, squash 1 px. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Held tremble: the same lean with a 1 px side jitter, eyes small and uncertain. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Eases: the body leans back toward upright, eyes wary but willing to face it. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Head ball tilts left 12 degrees while the body stays still, eyes squeezed. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Head ball tilts right 12 degrees. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Head ball tilts left 8 degrees again. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Back to centre with a small shrug-sag: body 1 px lower, eyes half-lidded and rueful. The pawn never speaks; this is its 'no, I may not'. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Strain begins: the body leans forward 10 degrees with the base planted, eyes narrowed with effort. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Pushing: lean 15 degrees with a 1 px effort shake to the right. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Straining harder: lean 18 degrees with a 1 px shake to the left, the whole body tense. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Bracing: lean 12 degrees, eyes bright and ready, loops back to frame 1. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Stands straighter: the body stretches 2 px, eyes widening. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
A soft pale-white 1 px rim glow around the whole outline, the body stretched 2 px. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Sways 6 degrees toward the restored direction and back, eyes bright. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Settles with a satisfied small squash, the glow fading. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.

poses_en: Stiff upright rest, base flat, body straight, eyes dull and watching. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
A slight 1 px sway to the left, the head ball 1 px lower. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
A slight 1 px sway to the right, body 1 px taller, eyes blink as thin horizontal lines for this frame only. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Squash: the body compresses 2 px and leans 5 degrees toward the facing direction. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Hop lift: the base is 2 px off the floor, body stretched 1 px, leaning 8 degrees forward. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Peak: the base is 2 px up, leaning 8 degrees, collar seam one shade brighter. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Land: the base is flat, squash 2 px, the lean returns to upright. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Notice: the head ball snaps toward the hero and the body rises 2 px, eyes brighten to dull red-orange, the collar seam lights. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Locked on: the raised posture holds with a tiny 1 px jolt, eyes steady and narrowed, the seam glowing dark orange (the anticipation orange, not red). VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Coil begins: the body leans back 8 degrees and twists 10 degrees to its left, squash 2 px, the seam turns dark orange. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Twist right: the body twists 10 degrees to its right so both diagonal corners of intent read, squash 2 px. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.

Maximum coil, held during the telegraph: compressed 2 px, leaning back 12 degrees, the seam glowing dark orange along the whole collar, eyes narrow slits. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Lunge: the body whips forward 2 px and tilts 15 degrees toward the front-left diagonal, the collar flares 1 px wider, the seam turning coral red. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.

IMPACT, the brightest frame: stretched 2 px, tilted 20 degrees toward the front-right diagonal, collar and seam bright coral red, thin white rim highlight. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Overshoot: leaning 10 degrees forward, the seam fading to dull red, the base slid 2 px forward. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Deflate: the body sags 2 px lower and tilts 8 degrees, the seam dark and dull, eyes half-lidded. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Slump: the deepest sag, 2 px, the head ball drooped, a 1 px wobble to the left. This is the readable punish window. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Rally: the body pulls back up to 1 px below rest, eyes sharpening, ready to return to idle. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Impact flash: every body pixel lightened toward white, the body squashed sideways (2 px wider, 2 px shorter), eyes squeezed shut. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Recoil: tilted 15 degrees away from the hit side, the base slid 2 px, eyes open wide, the red seam flickering. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Stagger: the body tilts 15 degrees, the seam flickering, eyes dim. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Tipping: tilt 40 degrees with the base lifted 2 px on one side, the red seam fading to grey. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Falling: tilt 70 degrees, the collar seam now matte, no glow left. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Floor impact: lying on its side with a small 2 px bounce; all red seams and eye glow gone, the paint matte and plain. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Settled: lying completely still as an ordinary toy pawn, the eyes now two plain painted dots; this is the pose left behind as the remains. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Reach: the body tilts 25 degrees forward toward a weapon lying on the floor in front, head ball lowered, eyes fixed on it. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Grab: the deepest tilt of 35 degrees, the front of the base lifting 1 px; the weapon itself is NOT drawn. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Rise armed: the body springs back upright stretched 1 px, eyes bright, seam glowing dark orange with satisfaction. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.

Marching away, step 1: seen from behind, the body squashes 2 px with the base rim pressing down, leaning 3 degrees away from the camera. VIEW: back view, the piece faces away from the camera (north); only the back of the head ball and body is visible, no face.

Step 2: the base 2 px off the floor, the body stretched 1 px, the plain back of the head ball bobbing 1 px. VIEW: back view, the piece faces away from the camera (north); only the back of the head ball and body is visible, no face.
Step 3: the base 2 px up, leaning 5 degrees away, calm and unhurried. VIEW: back view, the piece faces away from the camera (north); only the back of the head ball and body is visible, no face.

Step 4: landing with a 2 px squash, upright; loops to step 1. A tired, defeated-looking retreat, not an attack. VIEW: back view, the piece faces away from the camera (north); only the back of the head ball and body is visible, no face.

groups.title_vi: Tốt Đen biết lùi (Backstep)
groups.anchor: base-bottom centre at (16,30): the base rim sits on the line y=30 (the lowest drawn body row is y=29) with 2 px of empty canvas under it; every chess piece stands on this one anchor, so a shorter piece just leaves more empty canvas above its head
groups.subject_en: Backstep Pawn: a black-side chess pawn soldier of the Black army: a Staunton pawn with a round head ball, flat collar ring, tapering body and flared round base, charcoal with cool blue-black shadows and thin dull red seams along the collar and base rim, two small dull red eyes. The child's amendment 'may move backward' is scribbled on it in grey pencil: a small hand-drawn grey-pencil arrow pointing backward on the front of its base, and a tiny coiled spring-heel at the back of the base ring. It retreats after being hit and hops back before it strikes.
groups.details_en: Enemy clips are drawn in the FRONT view only; the game rotates or flips the sprite for other facings, and the separate back-view and side-view body stills carry the facing. The attack clip never plays for enemies: intent is shown by windup, commit and recover. The grey-pencil arrow is the variant's identity and stays visible in every frame (it is lighter and thinner than the outline, like a quick pencil scribble). CELL FIT (owner decision 2026-10-12: a chess piece is smaller than its cell). The canvas is 32x32, exactly one cell. The standing pawn body is at most 18x22 px, outline included, centred on x=16 with its base rim on y=30, so its top sits at y=8 and at least 2 px of empty canvas remain on every side: never exactly cell-sized, never taller than the cell, never touching or crossing a canvas edge. Relative heights follow a real chess set (pawn 22 px, knight, bishop and rook 24, queen 26, king 28; bosses on one cell are a little wider than their class and never beyond 24x28). In EVERY frame, squash, stretch, tilt, lean, lunge and lift included, every pixel of the piece stays inside x 2..29 and y 2..29: the headroom above the resting top is 6 px, a lift and a stretch together never use more than that, and a tilt or lean never pushes a side past x=2 or x=29; if a pose would not fit, shorten the stretch or the lift first and never the margin. The pixel measures written in the poses are already scaled to this body size.
groups.avoid_en: arms, legs, weapons drawn on the body (weapons are overlays), gore, blood, red anywhere except the dull seams and the commit flash, blue (blue is the child's colour), pure black or pure white fills, cartoon faces with mouths, floor shadows, effect sprites
groups.palette_en: Pencil mark #9A9AA3 (graphite grey) only for the scribbled arrow.
groups.notes_vi: Backstep: mũi tên bút chì xám viết tay trước đế (lời sửa luật của đứa trẻ) và lò xo nhỏ ở gót. Nó lùi sau khi bị đánh. Mốc dời về M6 vì T3/T4 (Act 1) đã đặt kẻ địch này (trước đây M9).

groups.title_vi: Tốt đồ chơi của Vua (blocker rồi kích hoạt)
groups.anchor: base-bottom centre at (16,30): the base rim sits on the line y=30 (the lowest drawn body row is y=29) with 2 px of empty canvas under it; every chess piece stands on this one anchor, so a shorter piece just leaves more empty canvas above its head
groups.subject_en: Toy Pawn Blocker: defeated Black pawns that the Black King restores through his 'Restore Formation' rule. Dormant, they are harmless matte grey-black toy pawns (cheap painted plastic, painted dot eyes) that only block cells; later they are ACTIVATED by red rule cracks and fight like Recruits.
groups.details_en: Enemy clips are drawn in the FRONT view only; the game rotates or flips the sprite for other facings, and the separate back-view and side-view body stills carry the facing. The attack clip never plays for enemies: intent is shown by windup, commit and recover. Two clearly different states must read at a glance: dormant toy (matte, flat, no glow) versus active (red cracks and eyes). The role set (alert, windup, commit, recover, hurt, defeat) is drawn in the ACTIVE look, the same poses as the Recruit. CELL FIT (owner decision 2026-10-12: a chess piece is smaller than its cell). The canvas is 32x32, exactly one cell. The standing pawn body is at most 18x22 px, outline included, centred on x=16 with its base rim on y=30, so its top sits at y=8 and at least 2 px of empty canvas remain on every side: never exactly cell-sized, never taller than the cell, never touching or crossing a canvas edge. Relative heights follow a real chess set (pawn 22 px, knight, bishop and rook 24, queen 26, king 28; bosses on one cell are a little wider than their class and never beyond 24x28). In EVERY frame, squash, stretch, tilt, lean, lunge and lift included, every pixel of the piece stays inside x 2..29 and y 2..29: the headroom above the resting top is 6 px, a lift and a stretch together never use more than that, and a tilt or lean never pushes a side past x=2 or x=29; if a pose would not fit, shorten the stretch or the lift first and never the margin. The pixel measures written in the poses are already scaled to this body size.
groups.avoid_en: arms, legs, weapons drawn on the body (weapons are overlays), gore, blood, red anywhere except the dull seams, the commit flash and, once ACTIVATED, its dull red cracks (#9C2F2A, brightening to coral only on a commit frame), blue (blue is the child's colour), pure black or pure white fills, cartoon faces with mouths, floor shadows, effect sprites
groups.palette_en: Dormant: grey-black plastic #3A3D45 mid, #52565F light, #24262C shadow. Active adds dull red cracks #9C2F2A (the Black pieces' seam red, brightening to coral #D84A3A only on a commit frame) and red eyes. Under-Bed mood: faint deep-purple tint #2B2236 in the shadows.
groups.notes_vi: Tốt đồ chơi của Vua: trạng thái ngủ là đồ chơi nhựa xám đen vô hại (chỉ chắn đường), kích hoạt thì nứt đỏ và đánh như Recruit.

groups.subject_en: Passant Wraith (deferred, recipe E1): a ghostly Black pawn that dashes two cells and slips past: a pale grey translucent pawn silhouette drawn like a sketchy graphite pencil outline, no solid base (it hovers and its lower edge dissolves into pencil smudge), two white dot eyes. groups.details_en: Enemy clips are drawn in the FRONT view only; the game rotates or flips the sprite for other facings, and the separate back-view and side-view body stills carry the facing. The attack clip never plays for enemies: intent is shown by windup, commit and recover. CELL FIT (owner decision 2026-10-12: a chess piece is smaller than its cell). The canvas is 32x32, exactly one cell. The standing pawn body is at most 18x22 px, outline included, centred on x=16 with its base rim on y=30, so its top sits at y=8 and at least 2 px of empty canvas remain on every side: never exactly cell-sized, never taller than the cell, never touching or crossing a canvas edge. Relative heights follow a real chess set (pawn 22 px, knight, bishop and rook 24, queen 26, king 28; bosses on one cell are a little wider than their class and never beyond 24x28). In EVERY frame, squash, stretch, tilt, lean, lunge and lift included, every pixel of the piece stays inside x 2..29 and y 2..29: the headroom above the resting top is 6 px, a lift and a stretch together never use more than that, and a tilt or lean never pushes a side past x=2 or x=29; if a pose would not fit, shorten the stretch or the lift first and never the margin. The pixel measures written in the poses are already scaled to this body size.
groups.avoid_en: arms, legs, weapons drawn on the body (weapons are overlays), gore, blood, red anywhere except the dull seams and the commit flash, blue (blue is the child's colour), pure black or pure white fills, cartoon faces with mouths, floor shadows, effect sprites
groups.palette_en: Ghost: pale grey #B9BBC4 fill at 70 percent, graphite outline #6F7078, white dot eyes. No red except a dull seam on commit.
groups.notes_vi: Biến thể hoãn (recipe E1). Bóng ma vẽ bằng bút chì xám, lơ lửng, lao 2 ô.

poses_en: Floating rest: the pale ghost-pawn hovers 2 px above the floor, outline drawn like a sketchy graphite pencil line, no base contact. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Drifts 1 px left and 1 px lower, the bottom of the body dissolving into a few pencil-smudge pixels. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Drifts 1 px right and 1 px higher, the two white dot eyes blink. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Gathers: the body compresses 2 px, the pencil outline thickens. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Glides: the whole body slides 2 px forward stretched 2 px, smudge pixels trailing. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Peak glide: stretched 2 px leaning 10 degrees, the trailing smudge 4 px long. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Re-forms: back to rest height, the outline sharpening. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Notice: the head ball snaps toward the hero and the body rises 2 px, eyes brighten to dull red-orange, the collar seam lights. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Locked on: the raised posture holds with a tiny 1 px jolt, eyes steady and narrowed, the seam glowing dark orange (the anticipation orange, not red). VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Coil begins: the body leans back 8 degrees and twists 10 degrees to its left, squash 2 px, the seam turns dark orange. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Twist right: the body twists 10 degrees to its right so both diagonal corners of intent read, squash 2 px. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.

Maximum coil, held during the telegraph: compressed 2 px, leaning back 12 degrees, the seam glowing dark orange along the whole collar, eyes narrow slits. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Lunge: the body whips forward 2 px and tilts 15 degrees toward the front-left diagonal, the collar flares 1 px wider, the seam turning coral red. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.

IMPACT, the brightest frame: stretched 2 px, tilted 20 degrees toward the front-right diagonal, collar and seam bright coral red, thin white rim highlight. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Overshoot: leaning 10 degrees forward, the seam fading to dull red, the base slid 2 px forward. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Deflate: the body sags 2 px lower and tilts 8 degrees, the seam dark and dull, eyes half-lidded. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Slump: the deepest sag, 2 px, the head ball drooped, a 1 px wobble to the left. This is the readable punish window. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Rally: the body pulls back up to 1 px below rest, eyes sharpening, ready to return to idle. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Impact flash: every body pixel lightened toward white, the body squashed sideways (2 px wider, 2 px shorter), eyes squeezed shut. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Recoil: tilted 15 degrees away from the hit side, the base slid 2 px, eyes open wide, the red seam flickering. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Flinch: the sketch outline wobbles and breaks into dashes. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
The body fades to 60 percent, pencil lines separating. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Smudging: the body dissolves into grey smudge pixels from the top down. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Only a faint grey smudge and a few eraser-crumb pixels remain. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Settled: a small grey pencil smudge with three eraser crumbs; nothing of the ghost remains. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Stretch: the body elongates 2 px forward in a smear of pencil lines, eyes narrowed. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Streak: a long horizontal pencil-line smear 2 cells long with the pale ghost at its head. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Arrive: the ghost re-forms at the end of the smear, a small smudge behind it. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.

groups.title_vi: Mã Đen (Tracker / Guard)
groups.anchor: pedestal base-bottom centre at (16,30): the base rim sits on the line y=30 (the lowest drawn body row is y=29) with 2 px of empty canvas under it; every chess piece stands on this one anchor, so a shorter piece just leaves more empty canvas above its head
groups.subject_en: Knight Tracker: a Black chess knight: a glossy charcoal horse head and arched neck in side profile on a round pedestal base (no body, no legs), like the owner-approved chess knight silhouette, a crimson mane ridge along the neck, a small red scarf seam at the base of the neck, one eye. It steps in L-shapes, telegraphs an outlined L with crosshair for 0.9 s, leaps and lands on the hero, then is left vulnerable for 1.2 s. Its body language is proud, edgy and quick; the head does the acting.
groups.details_en: Enemy clips are drawn in the FRONT view only; the game rotates or flips the sprite for other facings, and the separate back-view and side-view body stills carry the facing. The attack clip never plays for enemies: intent is shown by windup, commit and recover. The knight silhouette must follow the owner-approved chess knight (head facing left, one ear, brow, muzzle taper). Windup, commit and recover are told by the head and neck. leap_takeoff, airborne and land are the visible leap; the landing marker shadow is drawn elsewhere. CELL FIT (owner decision 2026-10-12: a chess piece is smaller than its cell). The canvas is 32x32, exactly one cell. The standing knight body is at most 20x24 px, outline included, centred on x=16 with its base rim on y=30, so its top sits at y=6 and at least 2 px of empty canvas remain on every side: never exactly cell-sized, never taller than the cell, never touching or crossing a canvas edge. Relative heights follow a real chess set (pawn 22 px, knight, bishop and rook 24, queen 26, king 28; bosses on one cell are a little wider than their class and never beyond 24x28). In EVERY frame, squash, stretch, tilt, lean, lunge and lift included, every pixel of the piece stays inside x 2..29 and y 2..29: the headroom above the resting top is 4 px, a lift and a stretch together never use more than that, and a tilt or lean never pushes a side past x=2 or x=29; if a pose would not fit, shorten the stretch or the lift first and never the margin. The pixel measures written in the poses are already scaled to this body size. In flight frames the art lifts the base by at most 2 px (the rest of the jump arc is the engine's, and the separate flight shadow shows the height).
groups.avoid_en: arms, legs, weapons drawn on the body (weapons are overlays), gore, blood, red anywhere except the dull seams and the commit flash, blue (blue is the child's colour), pure black or pure white fills, cartoon faces with mouths, floor shadows, effect sprites, legs, a rider, a visible spear or shield (weapons are overlays)
groups.palette_en: Mane ridge crimson #8E2A2A, neck scarf seam #9C2F2A.
groups.notes_vi: Mã Đen: đầu và cổ ngựa trên đế tròn như quân Mã thật (giống knight_idle đã duyệt), mọi diễn xuất nằm ở đầu và cổ. Clip leap gồm takeoff, airborne, land.

groups.title_vi: Mã Đen canh gác (Guard Knight, biến thể)
groups.anchor: pedestal base-bottom centre at (16,30): the base rim sits on the line y=30 (the lowest drawn body row is y=29) with 2 px of empty canvas under it; every chess piece stands on this one anchor, so a shorter piece just leaves more empty canvas above its head
groups.subject_en: Guard Knight (a deferred variant of the Knight Tracker): a Black chess knight: a glossy charcoal horse head and arched neck in side profile on a round pedestal base (no body, no legs), like the owner-approved chess knight silhouette, a crimson mane ridge along the neck, a small red scarf seam at the base of the neck, one eye. It stays near a weapon or objective, so it wears a small round wooden toy shield (with a faded painted red cross) hung at the base of the neck and a dull steel-grey bridle strap on the muzzle. Same attack as the Tracker; the look says 'on duty, not hunting'.
groups.details_en: Enemy clips are drawn in the FRONT view only; the game rotates or flips the sprite for other facings, and the separate back-view and side-view body stills carry the facing. The attack clip never plays for enemies: intent is shown by windup, commit and recover. CELL FIT (owner decision 2026-10-12: a chess piece is smaller than its cell). The canvas is 32x32, exactly one cell. The standing knight body is at most 20x24 px, outline included, centred on x=16 with its base rim on y=30, so its top sits at y=6 and at least 2 px of empty canvas remain on every side: never exactly cell-sized, never taller than the cell, never touching or crossing a canvas edge. Relative heights follow a real chess set (pawn 22 px, knight, bishop and rook 24, queen 26, king 28; bosses on one cell are a little wider than their class and never beyond 24x28). In EVERY frame, squash, stretch, tilt, lean, lunge and lift included, every pixel of the piece stays inside x 2..29 and y 2..29: the headroom above the resting top is 4 px, a lift and a stretch together never use more than that, and a tilt or lean never pushes a side past x=2 or x=29; if a pose would not fit, shorten the stretch or the lift first and never the margin. The pixel measures written in the poses are already scaled to this body size. In flight frames the art lifts the base by at most 2 px (the rest of the jump arc is the engine's, and the separate flight shadow shows the height).
groups.avoid_en: arms, legs, weapons drawn on the body (weapons are overlays), gore, blood, red anywhere except the dull seams, the commit flash and the faded painted red cross on the shield (#8E2A2A), blue (blue is the child's colour), pure black or pure white fills, cartoon faces with mouths, floor shadows, effect sprites

The head turns 2 px toward the hero, ready to loop to frame 1. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Crouch: the whole piece squashes 2 px, the head dipping, ready for an L-shaped hop. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Spring: the pedestal is 2 px off the floor, the head thrown forward, the neck stretched. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.

Land: squash 2 px, the head bobbing 1 px, settling. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.

Rally: the head lifting back toward the neutral height, the eye sharpening. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Impact flash: every pixel lightened toward white, the head thrown back 12 degrees, the piece squashed sideways, the eye squeezed shut. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.

Falling: tilt 65 degrees, the red seams fading to grey. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.

In EVERY frame, squash, stretch, tilt, lean, lunge and lift included, every pixel of the piece stays inside x 2..29 and y 2..29: the headroom above the resting top is 4 px, a lift and a stretch together never use more than that, and a tilt or lean never pushes a side past x=2 or x=29; if a pose would not fit, shorten the stretch or the lift first and never the margin. Stagger: tilt 12 degrees, the slit flickering. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Tipping: tilt 40 degrees with the base lifting 2 px, the slit fading to grey. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Falling: tilt 70 degrees, the mitre dropping, colours going matte. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Floor impact: lying on its side with a 2 px bounce, all glow gone. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Settled: lying still as an ordinary toy bishop piece, the slit now just a painted line; this is the pose left as the remains. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Channel begins: the mitre tilted 8 degrees along the diagonal, a 1 px red-orange glow at the base of the slit. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
The glow grows: 2 px of dark orange rising up the slit, the body trembling 1 px. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
The glow is 4 px tall and brighter, the body tilted 10 degrees, the tip of the mitre vibrating. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Full channel: the slit lit dark orange to its tip, the mitre pointing exactly along the lane, loops back to frame 1. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.

poses_en: Tall and calm: the mitre upright with its diagonal slit dark, the body straight, the base flat. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
The mitre sways 1 px to the left, a slow breath stretching the body 1 px. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
The mitre sways 1 px to the right, the slit catching a single dull red pixel for this frame only. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Squash: the body compresses 2 px and tilts 6 degrees toward the diagonal it will slide along. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Slide-hop: the base is 2 px up, the body tilted 10 degrees along the diagonal and stretched 1 px. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Peak: the base is 2 px up, the tilt 10 degrees, the slit one shade brighter. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Land: squash 2 px, back to upright. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Notice: the mitre snaps toward the hero, the slit lights dull red-orange, the body rises 2 px. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Locked: the mitre tilted 8 degrees along the diagonal toward the hero, the slit dark orange, calm and exact. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
The body tilts 8 degrees so the mitre points along the chosen diagonal, the slit lighting dark orange from the bottom. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Tilt 12 degrees, the slit glow rising along its length, the body squashing 1 px, eyes narrow. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.

Maximum tilt, held during the 0.8 s telegraph (the lane grows outward in the overlay): the slit glowing dark orange its full length, the body trembling 1 px. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Release: the mitre snaps upright and the body stretches 2 px, the slit turning coral red. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
IMPACT, the brightest frame: the whole slit blazing bright coral red with a thin white rim, the body at full stretch. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Fade: the body returns toward upright, the slit dying down to dull red. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Drained: the body sags 2 px, the slit dark, the mitre drooping 5 degrees. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Exposed: the deepest sag, 2 px, the mitre bowed, a slow 1 px wobble; this is the readable punish window. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Rally: standing back up to rest height, the slit sharpening. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Impact flash: every pixel lightened toward white, the mitre knocked sideways 10 degrees, the body squashed. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Recoil: tilted 15 degrees away from the hit, the base slid 2 px, the slit flickering red. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Stagger: tilt 12 degrees, the slit flickering. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Tipping: tilt 40 degrees with the base lifting 2 px, the slit fading to grey. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Falling: tilt 70 degrees, the mitre dropping, colours going matte. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Floor impact: lying on its side with a 2 px bounce, all glow gone. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Settled: lying still as an ordinary toy bishop piece, the slit now just a painted line; this is the pose left as the remains. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Channel begins: the mitre tilted 8 degrees along the diagonal, a 1 px red-orange glow at the base of the slit. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
The glow grows: 2 px of dark orange rising up the slit, the body trembling 1 px. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
The glow is 4 px tall and brighter, the body tilted 10 degrees, the tip of the mitre vibrating. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Full channel: the slit lit dark orange to its tip, the mitre pointing exactly along the lane, loops back to frame 1. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.

groups.title_vi: Xe Gỗ (Wooden Rook)
groups.anchor: base-bottom centre at (16,30): the base rim sits on the line y=30 (the lowest drawn body row is y=29) with 2 px of empty canvas under it; every chess piece stands on this one anchor, so a shorter piece just leaves more empty canvas above its head
groups.subject_en: Wooden Rook: a Black chess rook: a Staunton castle tower with a crenellated battlement crown (four square teeth), a slit visor band under the crown, a straight square-feeling body and a wide flared base, charcoal with cool blue-black shadows and a thin dull red seam under the battlement. It is a wooden toy rook painted black: the paint is chipped, pale wood grain shows at the battlement and base, and the wood has a faint grain texture. It declares a row or column, charges until blocked, and BREAKS after two collisions with obstacles: it has an intact look and a cracked look.
groups.details_en: Enemy clips are drawn in the FRONT view only; the game rotates or flips the sprite for other facings, and the separate back-view and side-view body stills carry the facing. The attack clip never plays for enemies: intent is shown by windup, commit and recover. Charge clips are drawn for south (toward the camera), north (away) and east (sideways); west is the east frames mirrored. In every charge frame the body is stretched along its travel axis. After its first collision the game switches to the cracked look: idle_cracked replaces idle; the other clips are reused. Its second collision plays the defeat clip (it breaks into blocks). CELL FIT (owner decision 2026-10-12: a chess piece is smaller than its cell). The canvas is 32x32, exactly one cell. The standing rook body is at most 20x24 px, outline included, centred on x=16 with its base rim on y=30, so its top sits at y=6 and at least 2 px of empty canvas remain on every side: never exactly cell-sized, never taller than the cell, never touching or crossing a canvas edge. Relative heights follow a real chess set (pawn 22 px, knight, bishop and rook 24, queen 26, king 28; bosses on one cell are a little wider than their class and never beyond 24x28). In EVERY frame, squash, stretch, tilt, lean, lunge and lift included, every pixel of the piece stays inside x 2..29 and y 2..29: the headroom above the resting top is 4 px, a lift and a stretch together never use more than that, and a tilt or lean never pushes a side past x=2 or x=29; if a pose would not fit, shorten the stretch or the lift first and never the margin. The pixel measures written in the poses are already scaled to this body size.
groups.avoid_en: arms, legs, weapons drawn on the body (weapons are overlays), gore, blood, red anywhere except the dull seams and the commit flash, blue (blue is the child's colour), pure black or pure white fills, cartoon faces with mouths, floor shadows, effect sprites, metal plates (that is the Iron Rook)
groups.palette_en: Wood showing through: #B58F63 grain, #7A5A38 shadow.
groups.notes_vi: Xe Gỗ: xe đồ chơi bằng gỗ sơn đen, bong tróc để lộ vân gỗ nhạt. Có hai dáng: nguyên vẹn và nứt (sau va chạm đầu). Va chạm lần 2 thì vỡ thành khối gỗ.

groups.subject_en: Black Pawn Captain (boss B1, 'Rank Breaker', pride in holding a line): a broad-based Black pawn, the biggest pawn on the board (a 24x22 px body box against 18x22 px for a common pawn) with a wide base ring: polished charcoal with cool blue-black shadows; a torn-edged red officer's cloth sash tied around the collar; pale bone ruler tick-marks engraved evenly around the base ring (the child's rules made metal); thin dull red seams along the collar and base; two narrow dull red eyes. Posture is rigid and proud and never slouches. He wields a ruler blade, which is a separate overlay and is never drawn on the body.
groups.details_en: Boss clips are drawn in the FRONT view only (the game flips or rotates the sprite for other facings, and the back-view and side-view body stills carry the facing). Boss size is per boss (owner decision 2026-10-13) and this boss stands on ONE cell: it is a chess piece like any other, smaller than its cell and drawn on the same 32x32 canvas as every piece (its body box is 24x22 px, a little wider than the common piece of its kind), and it reads as a boss through its crown, silhouette details, colours and the separate aura and burst effect files, not through size. The telegraph cells it threatens are drawn elsewhere, so no pose may hide the floor with effect sprites. Every clip is drawn in the phase look named in its pose text; do not blend looks. Three phase looks, each in front, back and side stills. The plain standing body still is the phase 1 look. CELL FIT (owner decisions 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-13: a chess piece is smaller than its cell, and a boss's size is per boss; this boss stands on one cell). The canvas is 32x32, exactly one cell. This boss's standing body is at most 24x22 px, outline included, centred on x=16 with its base rim on y=30, so its top sits at y=8 and at least 2 px of empty canvas remain on every side: never exactly cell-sized, never taller than the cell, never touching or crossing a canvas edge. Relative heights follow a real chess set (pawn 22 px, knight, bishop and rook 24, queen 26, king 28; bosses on one cell are a little wider than their class and never beyond 24x28). In EVERY frame, squash, stretch, tilt, lean, lunge and lift included, every pixel of the piece stays inside x 2..29 and y 2..29: the headroom above the resting top is 6 px, a lift and a stretch together never use more than that, and a tilt or lean never pushes a side past x=2 or x=29; if a pose would not fit, shorten the stretch or the lift first and never the margin. The pixel measures written in the poses are already scaled to this body size.
groups.avoid_en: gore, blood, a visible weapon on the body (weapons are overlays), blue (child's colour), golden yellow (interactable colour), red anywhere except the dull seams, the coral-red commit flash, the eyes and the torn officer's sash (matte cloth #A8322C), floor shadows, effect sprites, text, pure black or pure white fills
groups.palette_en: Sash red #A8322C (torn, matte cloth), ruler ticks pale bone #D8D2BE, exposed wood in phase 3 #B58F63.
groups.notes_vi: Ba dáng theo 3 giai đoạn: P1 ngay ngắn, P2 nghiêng người chuẩn bị thước, P3 trầy xước sash rách. Mỗi dáng có 3 ảnh tĩnh (thẳng, lưng, phải).

[P1 look: upright, neat sash] The eyes ignite dull red, the head ball lifting 1 px. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P1 look: upright, neat sash] He rises 2 px, the sash lifting, the seams brightening. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P1 look: upright, neat sash] The base slams down ('Nothing passes the rug's edge'): squash 2 px, the sash flung forward. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P1 look: upright, neat sash] The sash swings back and settles, the body steadying at rest height. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P1 look: upright, neat sash] Holds the authority pose: upright, chin of the head ball raised, the eyes calm. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P1 look: upright, neat sash] The authority pose, calm, perfectly upright. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P1 look: upright, neat sash] A slow breath: the body 1 px taller, the sash tail lifting 1 px. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P1 look: upright, neat sash] The breath out: the body 1 px lower than rest, the sash settling, the eyes blinking as thin lines. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P2 look: braced lean, tight sash] The authority pose, braced, leaning slightly forward. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P2 look: braced lean, tight sash] A slow breath: the body 1 px taller, the sash tail lifting 1 px. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P2 look: braced lean, tight sash] The breath out: the body 1 px lower than rest, the sash settling, the eyes blinking as thin lines. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P3 look: scuffed, torn sash, cracked collar] The authority pose, heaving, a little lower with each breath. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P3 look: scuffed, torn sash, cracked collar] A slow breath: the body 1 px taller, the sash tail lifting 1 px. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P3 look: scuffed, torn sash, cracked collar] The breath out: the body 1 px lower than rest, the sash settling, the eyes blinking as thin lines. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P1 to P2] Standing in the P1 look; the head ball turns toward the side where the ruler blade will appear. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P1 to P2] He reaches: the body leans 8 degrees to that side as if gripping something just out of the frame. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P1 to P2] He pulls it up: the body straightens with a 2 px stretch, the P2 forward lean beginning. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P1 to P2] He braces: the base widens 2 px, squash 2 px, the seams brightening. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P1 to P2] The sash is retied: a quick flare of the sash tails. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P1 to P2] Locks into the P2 look: the braced forward lean, the tight sash, brighter seams. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P2 to P3] A hard hit staggers him: the head jerks back 10 degrees, the body squashing. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P2 to P3] A crack forms across the collar, chips of paint flying. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P2 to P3] The sash tears into two ragged tails, the body shaking 1 px. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P2 to P3] Shudder: the whole body vibrating, pale wood showing at the base. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P2 to P3] Roar: the body rises and flares, the seams flaring bright, the chest out. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P2 to P3] Settles into the P3 look: scuffed, lower, heaving. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P3 look: scuffed, torn sash, cracked collar] The final hit: the body flashes white, the head ball thrown back, the sash tails snapping. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P3 look: scuffed, torn sash, cracked collar] The red seams flicker and go out one by one, the eyes dimming to plain dots. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P3 look: scuffed, torn sash, cracked collar] The body sags 2 px and tilts 10 degrees, the sash falling slack. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P3 look: scuffed, torn sash, cracked collar] He tilts 40 degrees, slowly, the base lifting 2 px, colours draining toward matte plastic. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P3 look: scuffed, torn sash, cracked collar] Floor impact: lying on his side with a heavy 2 px bounce, completely plain and matte. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P3 look: scuffed, torn sash, cracked collar] Lying still as an ordinary toy pawn: no seams, no glow, no sash, two plain painted dots for eyes. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.

groups.title_vi: Boss Mã Đội Trưởng: dáng theo giai đoạn
groups.anchor: pedestal base-bottom centre at (16,30): the base rim sits on the line y=30 (the lowest drawn body row is y=29) with 2 px of empty canvas under it; every chess piece stands on this one anchor, so a shorter piece just leaves more empty canvas above its head
groups.subject_en: Knight Captain (boss of the Toybox, pride in status: 'You cannot catch what leaps'): a Black chess knight, bulkier than a common knight (a 24x24 px body box against 20x24 px), made of head, arched neck and a round pedestal (no body, no legs), glossy charcoal with cool blue-black shadows, in side profile like the owner-approved chess knight silhouette; a braided crimson mane ridge, three pale bone chevron stripes painted on the pedestal collar (cavalry rank), a small red toy-train conductor's whistle hanging on a cord at the base of the neck, flared nostrils and one proud eye. The chin is always raised.
groups.details_en: Boss clips are drawn in the FRONT view only (the game flips or rotates the sprite for other facings, and the back-view and side-view body stills carry the facing). Boss size is per boss (owner decision 2026-10-13) and this boss stands on ONE cell: it is a chess piece like any other, smaller than its cell and drawn on the same 32x32 canvas as every piece (its body box is 24x24 px, a little wider than the common piece of its kind), and it reads as a boss through its crown, silhouette details, colours and the separate aura and burst effect files, not through size. The telegraph cells it threatens are drawn elsewhere, so no pose may hide the floor with effect sprites. Every clip is drawn in the phase look named in its pose text; do not blend looks. The phase 2 grey-pencil double outline is the visual of the Book rewriting itself mid-fight: it must be thin, scribbly and unmistakably 'drawn on', not a shadow. The plain standing body still is the phase 1 look. CELL FIT (owner decisions 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-13: a chess piece is smaller than its cell, and a boss's size is per boss; this boss stands on one cell). The canvas is 32x32, exactly one cell. This boss's standing body is at most 24x24 px, outline included, centred on x=16 with its base rim on y=30, so its top sits at y=6 and at least 2 px of empty canvas remain on every side: never exactly cell-sized, never taller than the cell, never touching or crossing a canvas edge. Relative heights follow a real chess set (pawn 22 px, knight, bishop and rook 24, queen 26, king 28; bosses on one cell are a little wider than their class and never beyond 24x28). In EVERY frame, squash, stretch, tilt, lean, lunge and lift included, every pixel of the piece stays inside x 2..29 and y 2..29: the headroom above the resting top is 4 px, a lift and a stretch together never use more than that, and a tilt or lean never pushes a side past x=2 or x=29; if a pose would not fit, shorten the stretch or the lift first and never the margin. The pixel measures written in the poses are already scaled to this body size.
groups.avoid_en: gore, blood, a visible weapon on the body (weapons are overlays), blue (child's colour), golden yellow (interactable colour), red anywhere except the dull seams, the coral-red commit flash, the eyes, the braided crimson mane (#8E2A2A) and the toy whistle (#B8362F), floor shadows, effect sprites, text, pure black or pure white fills
groups.palette_en: Mane #8E2A2A, chevrons #D8D2BE, whistle #B8362F, grey-pencil double outline #9A9AA3 (phase 2 only).
groups.notes_vi: Ba dáng: P1 kiêu hãnh, P2 có nét bút chì xám vẽ đôi ('Mã được đi hai lần'), P3 bờm dữ tợn.

Patterns: Single Landing (one locked L leap), Twin Landing (two leaps, the second marker revealed late), Track Feint (a fake before the real strike), Train Crossing (he whistles up the toy train across a row), Toybox Shake (phase 3 stomp). The leap clips (leap_takeoff, airborne, land) are the true landing displacement of the boss and are shared by all leap patterns. 'vulnerable_crouch' is this boss's recover clip. In flight frames the art lifts the base by at most 2 px (the rest of the jump arc is the engine's, and the separate flight shadow shows the height).

groups.notes_vi: Mã Đội Trưởng: 5 chiêu (hạ cánh đơn, đôi, giả động tác, còi tàu, lắc hộp đồ chơi) + clip nhảy dùng chung + tư thế quỵ (recover) sau khi đáp. Có thêm clip di chuyển `move` (loop 4 khung) để boss đổi ô một bước; bản theo giai đoạn move_p2/p3 (King thêm p4) là tùy chọn.

poses_en: [P1 look: proud, chin raised] The head lowers and the eye locks on the target cell, the body crouching 2 px. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P1 look: proud, chin raised] Rearing: the neck arches 2 px up, the head thrown back 15 degrees, the pedestal tilting back 5 degrees. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P1 look: proud, chin raised] Coil: crouched 2 px, the head dropped forward along the L toward the target, the eye dark orange. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P1 look: proud, chin raised] Held during the 0.85 s telegraph: compressed, quivering 1 px, the eye bright dark orange, nostrils flared. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P1 look: proud, chin raised] The strike lands: the head slams down and forward 2 px, the mane flaring, the eye turning coral red. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.

[P1 look: proud, chin raised] IMPACT, the brightest frame: the head at the target cell with the neck fully extended, a thin white rim, the eye bright coral red. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P1 look: proud, chin raised] Follow-through: the head 2 px past the impact point, the eye fading to dull red. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P2 look: grey-pencil double outline] The head lowers, the double outline separating by 2 px more than at rest as it gathers to leap twice. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P2 look: grey-pencil double outline] First paw-stamp: the pedestal lifts 2 px and slams, the double outline following a beat late. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P2 look: grey-pencil double outline] Second stamp: lifts 2 px and slams, the double outline now a full 2 px behind. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P2 look: grey-pencil double outline] Held: crouched 2 px, the double outline split 2 px behind and flickering, the eye dark orange. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P2 look: grey-pencil double outline] The first strike: the head snaps down, the double outline streaming 2 px behind. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.

[P2 look: grey-pencil double outline] The echo: the grey-pencil outline slams down a beat later, offset, the real figure rising already for the second landing. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P2 look: grey-pencil double outline] Follow-through: the double outline merging back into the figure, the eye fading. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P2 look: grey-pencil double outline] The head swings left 2 px as a fake, the eye locked left, the body not committing. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P2 look: grey-pencil double outline] The head snaps right 2 px, the neck arching, the pedestal tilting right. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P2 look: grey-pencil double outline] A false rear: the neck rising 2 px, the eye flaring, then abruptly lowering. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P2 look: grey-pencil double outline] Held during the 0.95 s telegraph: the head low and still, the eye dark orange, one nostril flare. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P2 look: grey-pencil double outline] The real strike comes from the other side: the head whips down and forward 2 px. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P2 look: grey-pencil double outline] IMPACT, the brightest frame: the head slammed at the target, a thin white rim, the eye coral red. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P2 look: grey-pencil double outline] Follow-through, the double outline lagging. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P3 look: wild mane, bright eye] The head rears back 20 degrees, the mane flaring wide, the whistle cord swinging. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P3 look: wild mane, bright eye] The head thrown high, the muzzle lifted to the sky, the whistle hanging at the muzzle. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P3 look: wild mane, bright eye] The whistle is at the lips: cheeks puffed, the eye wide and gleeful, the neck stretched. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P3 look: wild mane, bright eye] The whistle blast: the head shaking 1 px, the mane streaming, the pedestal squashed 2 px. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P3 look: wild mane, bright eye] Held: the head lowered with a satisfied glare, the eye bright dark orange, the whistle swinging. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P3 look: wild mane, bright eye] The head stabs down and sideways pointing along the track row, the eye coral red. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P3 look: wild mane, bright eye] IMPACT, the brightest frame: the neck fully extended along the row, thin white rim, the whistle flying out sideways. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P3 look: wild mane, bright eye] Settle: the head returning, the eye dull red, the whistle swinging back. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P3 look: wild mane, bright eye] A hoof-stamp of the pedestal: lifts 2 px and slams, the mane shaking. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P3 look: wild mane, bright eye] A second harder stamp, squash 2 px, the neck rattling. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P3 look: wild mane, bright eye] The whole figure shaking 2 px side to side, the eye bright and wild. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P3 look: wild mane, bright eye] Held: crouched low and trembling, the eye bright dark orange. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P3 look: wild mane, bright eye] The huge stomp: the pedestal slams down, squash 2 px, the mane flaring, the eye coral red. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P3 look: wild mane, bright eye] The shockwave: the figure bouncing 2 px up, the eye wide. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P3 look: wild mane, bright eye] Settle: back to rest height, the mane settling slowly, the eye dull red. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P1 look: proud, chin raised] Crouch: the whole figure squashes 2 px, the head dropped, the eye dark orange. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P1 look: proud, chin raised] Launch: the pedestal leaves the floor, the neck stretching up and forward 2 px higher than rest. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P1 look: proud, chin raised] Rising: the pedestal 2 px up, the head thrown forward, the mane streaming back, tilt 20 degrees. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.

[P1 look: proud, chin raised] Apex: the pedestal 2 px above the floor, the neck arched, the head tilted down toward the landing cell, the mane streaming (its landing shadow is a separate sprite). VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P1 look: proud, chin raised] Descent: the pedestal 2 px up, the head tilting further down, the eye bright. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P1 look: proud, chin raised] Touchdown: the pedestal slams the floor, squash 2 px, the head slamming down. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P1 look: proud, chin raised] Rebound: stretched 2 px, the head rising 2 px. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
[P1 look: proud, chin raised] Settle: squash 2 px then rest height. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.

[P1 look: proud, chin raised] Settle: the round pedestal flat on the floor, the figure squashed 2 px, the chin raised, the braided crimson mane ridge lying still, the whistle hanging straight on its cord. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.

[P1 look: proud, chin raised] Rock left: the pedestal rolls onto its left edge so the right edge lifts 2 px, the figure tilting 5 degrees to the left, the neck arching 2 px higher, the mane streaming out to the right. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.

[P1 look: proud, chin raised] Trot lift: the whole pedestal 2 px off the floor and level, the head thrust 2 px forward with the chin still raised, the whistle swinging out on its cord. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.

[P1 look: proud, chin raised] Rock right: the pedestal rolls onto its right edge so the left edge lifts 2 px, the figure tilting 5 degrees to the right, the mane flicking out to the left; the clip loops back to frame 1. groups.title_vi: Boss Mã Đội Trưởng: ra mắt, đứng, chuyển giai đoạn, gục thành ngựa gỗ
groups.anchor: pedestal base-bottom centre at (16,30): the base rim sits on the line y=30 (the lowest drawn body row is y=29) with 2 px of empty canvas under it; every chess piece stands on this one anchor, so a shorter piece just leaves more empty canvas above its head
groups.subject_en: Knight Captain (boss of the Toybox, pride in status: 'You cannot catch what leaps'): a Black chess knight, bulkier than a common knight (a 24x24 px body box against 20x24 px), made of head, arched neck and a round pedestal (no body, no legs), glossy charcoal with cool blue-black shadows, in side profile like the owner-approved chess knight silhouette; a braided crimson mane ridge, three pale bone chevron stripes painted on the pedestal collar (cavalry rank), a small red toy-train conductor's whistle hanging on a cord at the base of the neck, flared nostrils and one proud eye. The chin is always raised.
groups.details_en: Boss clips are drawn in the FRONT view only (the game flips or rotates the sprite for other facings, and the back-view and side-view body stills carry the facing). Boss size is per boss (owner decision 2026-10-13) and this boss stands on ONE cell: it is a chess piece like any other, smaller than its cell and drawn on the same 32x32 canvas as every piece (its body box is 24x24 px, a little wider than the common piece of its kind), and it reads as a boss through its crown, silhouette details, colours and the separate aura and burst effect files, not through size. The telegraph cells it threatens are drawn elsewhere, so no pose may hide the floor with effect sprites. Every clip is drawn in the phase look named in its pose text; do not blend looks. Defeat: he is not killed, he becomes an ordinary wooden toy horse on little wheels. The phase 1 to 2 transition is the Book rewriting itself in grey pencil mid-fight: show it as a drawing appearing, with the Knight's surprise. CELL FIT (owner decisions 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-13: a chess piece is smaller than its cell, and a boss's size is per boss; this boss stands on one cell). The canvas is 32x32, exactly one cell. This boss's standing body is at most 24x24 px, outline included, centred on x=16 with its base rim on y=30, so its top sits at y=6 and at least 2 px of empty canvas remain on every side: never exactly cell-sized, never taller than the cell, never touching or crossing a canvas edge. Relative heights follow a real chess set (pawn 22 px, knight, bishop and rook 24, queen 26, king 28; bosses on one cell are a little wider than their class and never beyond 24x28). In EVERY frame, squash, stretch, tilt, lean, lunge and lift included, every pixel of the piece stays inside x 2..29 and y 2..29: the headroom above the resting top is 4 px, a lift and a stretch together never use more than that, and a tilt or lean never pushes a side past x=2 or x=29; if a pose would not fit, shorten the stretch or the lift first and never the margin. The pixel measures written in the poses are already scaled to this body size. In flight frames the art lifts the base by at most 2 px (the rest of the jump arc is the engine's, and the separate flight shadow shows the height).
groups.avoid_en: gore, blood, a visible weapon on the body (weapons are overlays), blue (child's colour), golden yellow (interactable colour), red anywhere except the dull seams, the coral-red commit flash, the eyes, the braided crimson mane (#8E2A2A) and the toy whistle (#B8362F), floor shadows, effect sprites, text, pure black or pure white fills
groups.palette_en: Mane #8E2A2A, chevrons #D8D2BE, whistle #B8362F, grey-pencil double outline #9A9AA3 (phase 2 only).
groups.notes_vi: Chuyển giai đoạn 1 sang 2 là cuốn sách tự sửa luật bằng bút chì xám: nét bút hiện dần quanh Mã, Mã ngạc nhiên rồi nhếch mép. Gục xuống thành ngựa gỗ đồ chơi có bánh xe.

groups.title_vi: Boss Giáo chủ Tượng: ra mắt, đứng, chuyển giai đoạn, gục thành tượng gấp giấy
groups.anchor: base-bottom centre at (16,30): the base rim sits on the line y=30 (the lowest drawn body row is y=29) with 2 px of empty canvas under it; every chess piece stands on this one anchor, so a shorter piece just leaves more empty canvas above its head
groups.subject_en: Bishop Oracle (boss of the Bookshelf, faith in written lines: 'Every piece has a purpose'): a tall slim Black chess bishop (a 22x24 px body box, slimmer than the other bosses) with a deep pointed mitre whose diagonal slit glows dull red, the body wrapped in strips of pale printed book-page paper pasted on like a scribe's robe (tiny grey text lines and a thin red margin line down the front), a ruled-paper collar, calm closed-lid slit eyes. Serene and absolute; it believes only in what is written.
groups.details_en: Boss clips are drawn in the FRONT view only (the game flips or rotates the sprite for other facings, and the back-view and side-view body stills carry the facing). Boss size is per boss (owner decision 2026-10-13) and this boss stands on ONE cell: it is a chess piece like any other, smaller than its cell and drawn on the same 32x32 canvas as every piece (its body box is 22x24 px, a little wider than the common piece of its kind), and it reads as a boss through its crown, silhouette details, colours and the separate aura and burst effect files, not through size. The telegraph cells it threatens are drawn elsewhere, so no pose may hide the floor with effect sprites. Every clip is drawn in the phase look named in its pose text; do not blend looks. Defeat: the Oracle is not destroyed; it folds itself into an ordinary folded paper bishop toy (origami-like, off-white, a simple pencil-drawn face). Gentle. CELL FIT (owner decisions 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-13: a chess piece is smaller than its cell, and a boss's size is per boss; this boss stands on one cell). The canvas is 32x32, exactly one cell. This boss's standing body is at most 22x24 px, outline included, centred on x=16 with its base rim on y=30, so its top sits at y=6 and at least 2 px of empty canvas remain on every side: never exactly cell-sized, never taller than the cell, never touching or crossing a canvas edge. Relative heights follow a real chess set (pawn 22 px, knight, bishop and rook 24, queen 26, king 28; bosses on one cell are a little wider than their class and never beyond 24x28). In EVERY frame, squash, stretch, tilt, lean, lunge and lift included, every pixel of the piece stays inside x 2..29 and y 2..29: the headroom above the resting top is 4 px, a lift and a stretch together never use more than that, and a tilt or lean never pushes a side past x=2 or x=29; if a pose would not fit, shorten the stretch or the lift first and never the margin. The pixel measures written in the poses are already scaled to this body size.
groups.avoid_en: gore, blood, a visible weapon on the body (weapons are overlays), blue (child's colour), golden yellow (interactable colour), red anywhere except the dull seams, the coral-red commit flash and the eyes, floor shadows, effect sprites, text, pure black or pure white fills
groups.palette_en: Page paper #E7DEC8 with grey text #8C8A84 and a red margin line #A8322C, mirror stickers silver #C9CFD8. Never crayon blue.
groups.notes_vi: Gục xuống: Giáo chủ tự gập mình thành tượng Tượng bằng giấy đồ chơi (kiểu origami), có khuôn mặt vẽ bút chì đơn giản.
