groups.subject_en: Rook Warden (boss of the Block Tower, force and walls: 'The straight path is the only path'): a stout Black iron rook (a 56x52 px body box on a 64x64 canvas: in phases 1 and 2 the Warden fills a 2x2-cell footprint, four cells): riveted dark iron plating, a crenellated battlement crown with four square teeth and a tiny pennant stub, a slit visor under the crown glowing dull red, a flared fortress-like base, everything built from straight rectangular blocks. Heavy, square, immovable.
groups.details_en: Boss clips are drawn in the FRONT view only (the game flips or rotates the sprite for other facings, and the back-view and side-view body stills carry the facing). Boss size is per boss (owner decision 2026-10-13): in phases 1 and 2 the Rook Warden fills a footprint of 2x2 cells and is drawn on a 64x64 canvas (its body box is 56x52 px), still smaller than its footprint like every piece, and it reads as a boss through its footprint, crown, silhouette details, colours and the separate aura and burst effect files. The telegraph cells it threatens are drawn elsewhere, so no pose may hide the floor with effect sprites. Every clip is drawn in the phase look named in its pose text; do not blend looks. The silhouette is rectilinear; keep every edge square and the slit visor as the focal point. The plain standing body still is the phase 1 look. CELL FIT (owner decisions 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-13: a piece is smaller than its cells, and a boss's size is per boss). In phases 1 and 2 the Rook Warden fills a footprint of 2x2 cells, so the canvas is 64x64, exactly four cells. This boss's standing body is at most 56x52 px, outline included, centred on x=32 with its base rim on y=62 (the lowest drawn body row is y=61, so 2 px of empty canvas remain under it, near the bottom of the footprint), so its top sits at y=10 and at least 2 px of empty canvas remain on every side (4 px at the left and the right): never exactly footprint-sized, never taller than the footprint, never touching or crossing a canvas edge. In EVERY frame, squash, stretch, tilt, lean, lunge and lift included, every pixel of the piece stays inside x 2..61 and y 2..61: the headroom above the resting top is 8 px, a lift and a stretch together never use more than that, and a tilt or lean never pushes a side past x=2 or x=61; if a pose would not fit, shorten the stretch or the lift first and never the margin. The pixel measures written in the poses are already scaled to this body size.
groups.avoid_en: gore, blood, a visible weapon on the body (weapons are overlays), blue (child's colour), golden yellow (interactable colour), red anywhere except the dull seams, the coral-red commit flash and the eyes, floor shadows, effect sprites, text, pure black or pure white fills
groups.palette_en: Iron: #3C4350 mid, #5C6677 light, #20242E shadow, rivets #8D96A6; the pennant stub #8E2A2A.
groups.notes_vi: Giai đoạn 1 và 2 chiếm 2x2 ô: P1 giáp sạch, P2 thêm tấm giáp dày phía trước. Mỗi dáng 3 ảnh tĩnh (thẳng, lưng, phải). Dáng giai đoạn 3 (1 ô, 32x32) nằm ở nhóm riêng vì một nhóm chỉ có một canvas.

groups.subject_en: Rook Warden (boss of the Block Tower, force and walls: 'The straight path is the only path'): a stout Black iron rook (a 24x24 px body box, as wide as a boss may be; in phase 3, after it breaks its own throne, the Warden has shrunk to one cell): riveted dark iron plating, a crenellated battlement crown with four square teeth and a tiny pennant stub, a slit visor under the crown glowing dull red, a flared fortress-like base, everything built from straight rectangular blocks. Heavy, square, immovable.
groups.details_en: Boss clips are drawn in the FRONT view only (the game flips or rotates the sprite for other facings, and the back-view and side-view body stills carry the facing). Boss size is per boss (owner decision 2026-10-13): in phase 3, after it breaks its own throne, the Rook Warden has shrunk from its 2x2-cell footprint to ONE cell, so here it is a chess piece like any other, smaller than its cell and drawn on the same 32x32 canvas as every piece (its body box is 24x24 px, a little wider than the common piece of its kind), and it reads as a boss through its crown, silhouette details, colours and the separate aura and burst effect files, not through size. The telegraph cells it threatens are drawn elsewhere, so no pose may hide the floor with effect sprites. Every clip is drawn in the phase look named in its pose text; do not blend looks. The silhouette is rectilinear; keep every edge square and the slit visor as the focal point. Patterns: Refuse To Turn (phase 3: he will not turn, so the player stands so the charge smashes the throne behind the lane). Charge clips are drawn for south, north and east (west is a tool mirror) and must stretch the body along the travel axis. The `move_p3` clip is the one-cell reposition loop (4 frames, loop, 8 fps, drawn in the P3 look): the engine plays it while the boss slides to the next cell, and that slide is code, never drawn, so the base never travels more than 3 px inside the canvas. CELL FIT (owner decisions 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-13: a chess piece is smaller than its cell, and a boss's size is per boss; in phase 3 the Warden stands on one cell). The canvas is 32x32, exactly one cell. This boss's standing body is at most 24x24 px, outline included, centred on x=16 with its base rim on y=30, so its top sits at y=6 and at least 2 px of empty canvas remain on every side: never exactly cell-sized, never taller than the cell, never touching or crossing a canvas edge. Relative heights follow a real chess set (pawn 22 px, knight, bishop and rook 24, queen 26, king 28; bosses on one cell are a little wider than their class and never beyond 24x28). In EVERY frame, squash, stretch, tilt, lean, lunge and lift included, every pixel of the piece stays inside x 2..29 and y 2..29: the headroom above the resting top is 4 px, a lift and a stretch together never use more than that, and a tilt or lean never pushes a side past x=2 or x=29; if a pose would not fit, shorten the stretch or the lift first and never the margin. The pixel measures written in the poses are already scaled to this body size.
groups.avoid_en: gore, blood, a visible weapon on the body (weapons are overlays), blue (child's colour), golden yellow (interactable colour), red anywhere except the dull seams, the coral-red commit flash and the eyes, floor shadows, effect sprites, text, pure black or pure white fills

groups.subject_en: Rook Warden (boss of the Block Tower, force and walls: 'The straight path is the only path'): a stout Black iron rook (a 24x24 px body box, as wide as a boss may be; in phase 3, after it breaks its own throne, the Warden has shrunk to one cell): riveted dark iron plating, a crenellated battlement crown with four square teeth and a tiny pennant stub, a slit visor under the crown glowing dull red, a flared fortress-like base, everything built from straight rectangular blocks. Heavy, square, immovable.
groups.details_en: Boss clips are drawn in the FRONT view only (the game flips or rotates the sprite for other facings, and the back-view and side-view body stills carry the facing). Boss size is per boss (owner decision 2026-10-13): in phase 3, after it breaks its own throne, the Rook Warden has shrunk from its 2x2-cell footprint to ONE cell, so here it is a chess piece like any other, smaller than its cell and drawn on the same 32x32 canvas as every piece (its body box is 24x24 px, a little wider than the common piece of its kind), and it reads as a boss through its crown, silhouette details, colours and the separate aura and burst effect files, not through size. The telegraph cells it threatens are drawn elsewhere, so no pose may hide the floor with effect sprites. Every clip is drawn in the phase look named in its pose text; do not blend looks. The silhouette is rectilinear; keep every edge square and the slit visor as the focal point. Defeat: the Warden is not destroyed; his iron comes apart into plain painted wooden toy blocks that form a small toy castle. Gentle, no gore. CELL FIT (owner decisions 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-13: a chess piece is smaller than its cell, and a boss's size is per boss; in phase 3 the Warden stands on one cell). The canvas is 32x32, exactly one cell. This boss's standing body is at most 24x24 px, outline included, centred on x=16 with its base rim on y=30, so its top sits at y=6 and at least 2 px of empty canvas remain on every side: never exactly cell-sized, never taller than the cell, never touching or crossing a canvas edge. Relative heights follow a real chess set (pawn 22 px, knight, bishop and rook 24, queen 26, king 28; bosses on one cell are a little wider than their class and never beyond 24x28). In EVERY frame, squash, stretch, tilt, lean, lunge and lift included, every pixel of the piece stays inside x 2..29 and y 2..29: the headroom above the resting top is 4 px, a lift and a stretch together never use more than that, and a tilt or lean never pushes a side past x=2 or x=29; if a pose would not fit, shorten the stretch or the lift first and never the margin. The pixel measures written in the poses are already scaled to this body size.
groups.avoid_en: gore, blood, a visible weapon on the body (weapons are overlays), blue (child's colour), golden yellow (interactable colour), red anywhere except the dull seams, the coral-red commit flash and the eyes, floor shadows, effect sprites, text, pure black or pure white fills

groups.title_vi: Boss Nữ hoàng: trỗi dậy, đứng, chuyển giai đoạn, gục thành quân Hậu đồ chơi
groups.anchor: base-bottom centre at (16,30): the base rim sits on the line y=30 (the lowest drawn body row is y=29) with 2 px of empty canvas under it; every chess piece stands on this one anchor, so a shorter piece just leaves more empty canvas above its head
groups.subject_en: Queen of Tricks (boss of the Dollhouse, sincere fear that a world without rules is forgotten; she offers the pawn promotion as being kept): a glossy Black chess queen (a 24x26 px body box, taller than the minor-piece bosses) with a crown of five balls (each ball tipped with a faint red glint), ornate but symmetrical and readable: a ruff of pale doll-lace around the neck, small plum-mauve ribbon bows at the crown base (dollhouse wallpaper colours), a tapering body and wide flared base; two small soft-lidded dot eyes that carry real sincerity and fear behind the authority; thin dull red seams at the neck. She is the antagonist with the most human face: never a monster.
groups.details_en: Boss clips are drawn in the FRONT view only (the game flips or rotates the sprite for other facings, and the back-view and side-view body stills carry the facing). Boss size is per boss (owner decision 2026-10-13) and this boss stands on ONE cell: it is a chess piece like any other, smaller than its cell and drawn on the same 32x32 canvas as every piece (its body box is 24x26 px, a little wider than the common piece of its kind), and it reads as a boss through its crown, silhouette details, colours and the separate aura and burst effect files, not through size. The telegraph cells it threatens are drawn elsewhere, so no pose may hide the floor with effect sprites. Every clip is drawn in the phase look named in its pose text; do not blend looks. The Queen animates less often than other pieces but with greater authority: fewer, slower, larger movements. Defeat: she lies down gently and becomes an ordinary plastic toy queen piece, the crown ball rolled aside, a pink ribbon bow beside her. Tender, not violent. CELL FIT (owner decisions 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-13: a chess piece is smaller than its cell, and a boss's size is per boss; this boss stands on one cell). The canvas is 32x32, exactly one cell. This boss's standing body is at most 24x26 px, outline included, centred on x=16 with its base rim on y=30, so its top sits at y=4 and at least 2 px of empty canvas remain on every side: never exactly cell-sized, never taller than the cell, never touching or crossing a canvas edge. Relative heights follow a real chess set (pawn 22 px, knight, bishop and rook 24, queen 26, king 28; bosses on one cell are a little wider than their class and never beyond 24x28). In EVERY frame, squash, stretch, tilt, lean, lunge and lift included, every pixel of the piece stays inside x 2..29 and y 2..29: the headroom above the resting top is 2 px, a lift and a stretch together never use more than that, and a tilt or lean never pushes a side past x=2 or x=29; if a pose would not fit, shorten the stretch or the lift first and never the margin. The pixel measures written in the poses are already scaled to this body size. Only 2 px of headroom exist: a stretch or a lift may use at most 2 px in total, and a lift of the base is paid for by squashing the body.
groups.avoid_en: gore, blood, a visible weapon on the body (weapons are overlays), blue (child's colour), golden yellow (interactable colour), red anywhere except the dull seams, the coral-red commit flash and the eyes, floor shadows, effect sprites, text, pure black or pure white fills
groups.palette_en: Dollhouse touches: lace #E8DFD0, ribbon plum-mauve #7A4A68, threads tan #C8B48E, crown glints #C0443C. No golden yellow, no blue.
groups.notes_vi: Gục xuống rất nhẹ nhàng: Nữ hoàng nằm xuống thành quân Hậu nhựa đồ chơi, vương miện lăn ra một bên, có nơ hồng bên cạnh.

The telegraph cells it threatens are drawn elsewhere, so no pose may hide the floor with effect sprites. Every clip is drawn in the phase look named in its pose text; do not blend looks. The plain standing body still is the phase 1 look. CELL FIT (owner decisions 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-13: a chess piece is smaller than its cell, and a boss's size is per boss; this boss stands on one cell). The canvas is 32x32, exactly one cell. This boss's standing body is at most 24x28 px, outline included, centred on x=16 with its base rim on y=30, so its top sits at y=2 and at least 2 px of empty canvas remain on every side: never exactly cell-sized, never taller than the cell, never touching or crossing a canvas edge. Relative heights follow a real chess set (pawn 22 px, knight, bishop and rook 24, queen 26, king 28; bosses on one cell are a little wider than their class and never beyond 24x28). In EVERY frame, squash, stretch, tilt, lean, lunge and lift included, every pixel of the piece stays inside x 2..29 and y 2..29: the headroom above the resting top is 0 px, a lift and a stretch together never use more than that, and a tilt or lean never pushes a side past x=2 or x=29; if a pose would not fit, shorten the stretch or the lift first and never the margin. The pixel measures written in the poses are already scaled to this body size. This body's 28 px is its full height and it has no headroom: a stooped, crouched or squashed pose stands lower and may rise back up to 28 px but never past it; a pose that says taller, stretched or rising, or that lifts the base, is drawn by squashing the body by the same amount (the top stays at y=2) or, when the body is already at full height, by widening and by cape, crown and finial details; the piece never leaves the margin. The phase 1 stoop stands 4 px below full height (a 24 px tall body, top at y=6, base on y=30); phases 2 to 4 stand at the full 28 px.

The pixel measures written in the poses are already scaled to this body size. This body's 28 px is its full height and it has no headroom: a stooped, crouched or squashed pose stands lower and may rise back up to 28 px but never past it; a pose that says taller, stretched or rising, or that lifts the base, is drawn by squashing the body by the same amount (the top stays at y=2) or, when the body is already at full height, by widening and by cape, crown and finial details; the piece never leaves the margin. groups.title_vi: Boss Vua Đen: ra mắt, đứng, chuyển giai đoạn, gục thành quân Vua đồ chơi
groups.anchor: base-bottom centre at (16,30): the base rim sits on the line y=30 (the lowest drawn body row is y=29) with 2 px of empty canvas under it; every chess piece stands on this one anchor, so a shorter piece just leaves more empty canvas above its head
groups.subject_en: Black King (final boss of the Under-Bed, 'The rules are mine'): a Black chess king (a 24x28 px body box, the tallest piece in the game) with a cross finial on a crown ball, polished charcoal, a slightly hollow body: red magical cracks run through the chest and collar and show tiny springs and gear teeth inside, small white rule cards with grey pencil lines tucked into the collar like pocket cards, thin pale eye slits, no mouth except a thin red crack. A rule system pretending to be a person: stiff, mannequin-like, authoritative; deep purple chess-box felt in the shadows.
groups.details_en: Boss clips are drawn in the FRONT view only (the game flips or rotates the sprite for other facings, and the back-view and side-view body stills carry the facing). Boss size is per boss (owner decision 2026-10-13) and this boss stands on ONE cell: it is a chess piece like any other, smaller than its cell and drawn on the same 32x32 canvas as every piece (its body box is 24x28 px, a little wider than the common piece of its kind), and it reads as a boss through its crown, silhouette details, colours and the separate aura and burst effect files, not through size. The telegraph cells it threatens are drawn elsewhere, so no pose may hide the floor with effect sprites. Every clip is drawn in the phase look named in its pose text; do not blend looks. Defeat is the climax: the cracks go out, the felt falls away and he becomes an ordinary toy king piece; the box opens and the pieces become toys again. It must feel like release, not violence. CELL FIT (owner decisions 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-13: a chess piece is smaller than its cell, and a boss's size is per boss; this boss stands on one cell). The canvas is 32x32, exactly one cell. This boss's standing body is at most 24x28 px, outline included, centred on x=16 with its base rim on y=30, so its top sits at y=2 and at least 2 px of empty canvas remain on every side: never exactly cell-sized, never taller than the cell, never touching or crossing a canvas edge. Relative heights follow a real chess set (pawn 22 px, knight, bishop and rook 24, queen 26, king 28; bosses on one cell are a little wider than their class and never beyond 24x28). In EVERY frame, squash, stretch, tilt, lean, lunge and lift included, every pixel of the piece stays inside x 2..29 and y 2..29: the headroom above the resting top is 0 px, a lift and a stretch together never use more than that, and a tilt or lean never pushes a side past x=2 or x=29; if a pose would not fit, shorten the stretch or the lift first and never the margin. The pixel measures written in the poses are already scaled to this body size. This body's 28 px is its full height and it has no headroom: a stooped, crouched or squashed pose stands lower and may rise back up to 28 px but never past it; a pose that says taller, stretched or rising, or that lifts the base, is drawn by squashing the body by the same amount (the top stays at y=2) or, when the body is already at full height, by widening and by cape, crown and finial details; the piece never leaves the margin. The phase 1 stoop stands 4 px below full height (a 24 px tall body, top at y=6, base on y=30); phases 2 to 4 stand at the full 28 px.
groups.avoid_en: gore, blood, a visible weapon on the body (weapons are overlays), blue (child's colour), golden yellow (interactable colour), red anywhere except the dull seams, the coral-red commit flash, the eyes, the red rule cracks, the gear glow and the finial cross (ember red #B8362F at rest), floor shadows, effect sprites, text, pure black or pure white fills, golden yellow

groups.title_vi: Cỗ máy Luật (Rule Engine) trong phòng boss Vua, chiếm 3x3 ô (canvas 96x96)
groups.anchor: base-bottom centre at (48,94): the base rim sits on the line y=94 (the lowest drawn body row is y=93) with 2 px of empty canvas under it, near the bottom of the 3x3-cell footprint
groups.subject_en: The Rule Engine: the machine that rewrites the tiles and controls the final fight. A squat clockwork cabinet built from a giant chess box: dark purple felt panels, iron clasps, a big toothed gear wheel on top, a hopper slot where rule cards go in (tiny card slots along its front), springs coiled at both sides, and glowing red crack-lines running through its panels. The King stays near it; it can be struck during the King's recovery. It fills a footprint of 3x3 cells: a 96x96 canvas, three cells wide and three cells deep.
groups.details_en: Machine pixel art at 1x1 with a near-black 1 px outline outside, three flat shading bands per material, no gradients, no dithering. Front view only. The machine does not move across the floor; only its gear, springs and glow animate. The Rule Engine never moves (it cannot teleport and has no step), so it has no move clip on purpose. CELL FIT (owner decision 2026-10-13: boss size is per boss, and the Rule Engine machine behind the Black King fills 3x3 cells). The canvas is 96x96, exactly nine cells. The machine is not a chess piece but it follows the same rule as one: its body, outline included, is at most 92x92 px (the intended squat cabinet is about 88 px wide and 80 px tall), centred on x=48 with its base rim on y=94 (the lowest drawn body row is y=93, so 2 px of empty canvas remain under it, near the bottom of the footprint), and at least 2 px of empty canvas remain on every side: never exactly footprint-sized, never touching or crossing a canvas edge. In EVERY frame, vibration, popped lid, flying card, stretched springs and flash included, every pixel of the machine stays inside x 2..93 and y 2..93. The cabinet has room for individual rivets, felt weave, card-slot edges and single gear teeth: draw them.
groups.avoid_en: gore, blood, a visible weapon on the body (weapons are overlays), blue (child's colour), golden yellow (interactable colour), red anywhere except the dull seams, the coral-red commit flash, the eyes, the red crack-lines and the gear glow (ember red #B8362F at rest), floor shadows, effect sprites, text, pure black or pure white fills, golden yellow, a face
groups.palette_en: Felt deep purple #2B2236 and #3A2D49, iron #3C4350 with highlights #5C6677, cracks ember red #B8362F (brightening to coral #D84A3A only on a commit frame), gear glow ember red #B8362F, card slots pale #E9E4D6, near-black outline #14141C.
groups.notes_vi: Cỗ máy làm từ hộp cờ khổng lồ: nỉ tím, khóa sắt, bánh răng lớn, khe nhận thẻ luật, lò xo, vết nứt đỏ. Có 3 trạng thái: ngủ, hoạt động, quá tải (lúc Vua kiệt sức). Chiếm 3x3 ô (canvas 96x96), thân gọn trong đó chừa ít nhất 2 px mỗi cạnh, đế sát đáy.

groups.title_vi: Sáu boss: xác thành đồ chơi bình thường (ảnh tĩnh)
groups.anchor: feet/base centre of the object at (16,30): the toy rests on the line y=30 with 2 px of empty canvas under it
groups.subject_en: The permanent resting state of each defeated boss: not a corpse, an ordinary toy again. Bosses are 'defeated, not killed': the broken pieces become ordinary toys. Each image is one small object lying on the floor, centred on the 32x32 canvas of one cell, drawn smaller than the live boss (at most 24x20 px) with matte plastic, wood or paper materials, no seams, no glow, no red, and a gentle, slightly sad feeling.
groups.details_en: Small simple toy object, near-black 1 px outline outside the silhouette, three flat shading bands, no gradients, no dithering, transparent background, no ground shadow, nothing else on the canvas. CELL FIT (owner decision 2026-10-12: a chess piece is smaller than its cell). The canvas is 32x32, exactly one cell. A piece lying on its side is its standing body box turned 90 degrees: each toy is at most 24x20 px, smaller than the live boss it was, and it matches the last frame of that boss's defeat clip on the same 32x32 canvas. Outline included, it rests on the line y=30 and is centred on x=16, so at least 2 px of empty canvas remain on every side and nothing touches or crosses a canvas edge; a tilted or half-fallen piece keeps its whole silhouette inside x 2..29 and y 2..29.
groups.avoid_en: gore, blood, glowing parts, red cracks, any hint of life, effect sprites, text
groups.palette_en: Matte toy materials: plastic black #2E323C, painted wood #B58F63, paper #E7DEC8, felt #3A2D49, ribbon plum-mauve #7A4A68.
groups.notes_vi: Sáu món đồ chơi bình thường còn lại sau khi boss bị đánh bại (và hộp cờ mở của Cỗ máy Luật). Mỗi ảnh một vật nhỏ nằm giữa khung, vật liệu nhựa, gỗ, giấy, không phát sáng.

groups.title_vi: Quân trắng được giải cứu: Pebble (Mã trắng)
groups.anchor: pedestal base-bottom centre at (16,30): the base rim sits on the line y=30 (the lowest drawn body row is y=29) with 2 px of empty canvas under it; every chess piece stands on this one anchor, so a shorter piece just leaves more empty canvas above its head
groups.subject_en: Pebble, a white Knight (rescue 1 in the hub, fear of being put away): a small ivory chess knight made of head, arched neck and a round pedestal (no body, no legs), in the owner-approved knight silhouette, a mended pale blue-grey cloth patch on the neck stitched with two tiny stitches (matching the hero pawn's tie), a nicked ear, a soft ivory mane ridge, big round dark eyes. A timid, sweet, worried piece.
groups.details_en: The white side is warm ivory with pale blue-grey shadows and mended seams, rounded and gentle; these pieces are survivors, scuffed and patched, never royal or glamorous. Three story states (trapped, freed, hub resident) plus the clips between them. The rescue is a hold-E beat of about 1.5 s: the four progress frames are shown in order while the player holds E. OWNERSHIP RULE: the trap (block, ribbon or cage) is owned ONLY by a separate trap prop file, which is layered in FRONT of this sprite on the same canvas with the same anchor. No file and no frame of this group ever draws any part of the trap, so the owner can swap the piece and its trap independently and the two never show two different traps stacked on each other. CELL FIT (owner decision 2026-10-12: a chess piece is smaller than its cell). The canvas is 32x32, exactly one cell. The standing knight body is at most 20x24 px, outline included, centred on x=16 with its base rim on y=30, so its top sits at y=6 and at least 2 px of empty canvas remain on every side: never exactly cell-sized, never taller than the cell, never touching or crossing a canvas edge. Relative heights follow a real chess set (pawn 22 px, knight, bishop and rook 24, queen 26, king 28; bosses on one cell are a little wider than their class and never beyond 24x28). In EVERY frame, squash, stretch, tilt, lean, lunge and lift included, every pixel of the piece stays inside x 2..29 and y 2..29: the headroom above the resting top is 4 px, a lift and a stretch together never use more than that, and a tilt or lean never pushes a side past x=2 or x=29; if a pose would not fit, shorten the stretch or the lift first and never the margin. The pixel measures written in the poses are already scaled to this body size.
groups.avoid_en: arms, legs, weapons, a crown, gore, blood, red (white pieces are never red), crayon blue (child's colour), pure white fills, floor shadows, effect sprites, text, any mouth
groups.palette_en: Shared palette of the style block.
groups.notes_vi: Pebble: Mã trắng nhỏ, nhút nhát. Sprite KẸT chỉ vẽ con cờ trần đang co rúm; khối gỗ đè nằm ở prop rescue_trap_pebble (vẽ phủ lên trước). 3 trạng thái: kẹt, được cứu, cư dân hub. Có clip 'bark' (nói một câu).

The head turning 2 px toward the hero; loops to frame 1. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
The head lifts 2 px and the ears perk up as it is about to speak. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
The head bobs forward 2 px (the 'speaking' beat), the eye bright and earnest. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.

groups.title_vi: Quân trắng được giải cứu: Stout (Xe trắng)
groups.anchor: base-bottom centre at (16,30): the base rim sits on the line y=30 (the lowest drawn body row is y=29) with 2 px of empty canvas under it; every chess piece stands on this one anchor, so a shorter piece just leaves more empty canvas above its head
groups.subject_en: Stout, a white Rook (rescue 3 in the Block Tower, 'always fell in line'): a sturdy ivory chess rook with four battlement teeth, one tooth chipped, a pale blue-grey scarf at the neck with a stitched patch, round dark eyes under the battlement, a straight stiff stance that looks used to being told where to stand.
groups.details_en: The white side is warm ivory with pale blue-grey shadows and mended seams, rounded and gentle; these pieces are survivors, scuffed and patched, never royal or glamorous. Three story states (trapped, freed, hub resident) plus the clips between them. The rescue is a hold-E beat of about 1.5 s: the four progress frames are shown in order while the player holds E. OWNERSHIP RULE: the trap (block, ribbon or cage) is owned ONLY by a separate trap prop file, which is layered in FRONT of this sprite on the same canvas with the same anchor. No file and no frame of this group ever draws any part of the trap, so the owner can swap the piece and its trap independently and the two never show two different traps stacked on each other. CELL FIT (owner decision 2026-10-12: a chess piece is smaller than its cell). The canvas is 32x32, exactly one cell. The standing rook body is at most 20x24 px, outline included, centred on x=16 with its base rim on y=30, so its top sits at y=6 and at least 2 px of empty canvas remain on every side: never exactly cell-sized, never taller than the cell, never touching or crossing a canvas edge. Relative heights follow a real chess set (pawn 22 px, knight, bishop and rook 24, queen 26, king 28; bosses on one cell are a little wider than their class and never beyond 24x28). In EVERY frame, squash, stretch, tilt, lean, lunge and lift included, every pixel of the piece stays inside x 2..29 and y 2..29: the headroom above the resting top is 4 px, a lift and a stretch together never use more than that, and a tilt or lean never pushes a side past x=2 or x=29; if a pose would not fit, shorten the stretch or the lift first and never the margin. The pixel measures written in the poses are already scaled to this body size.
groups.avoid_en: arms, legs, weapons, a crown, gore, blood, red (white pieces are never red), crayon blue (child's colour), pure white fills, floor shadows, effect sprites, text, any mouth

groups.anchor: centre of the floor-contact line at (16,30): the lying piece rests on the line y=30 (its lowest drawn row is y=29) with 2 px of empty canvas under it, centred on x=16
groups.subject_en: The fallen white King, the dead focal point of room T1 (the war is lost): a large ivory chess king lying on its side, toppled, the cross finial on its crown ball slightly bent, a small hairline crack down the body, scuffed and tired. His base faces the camera and is worn completely smooth in one patch as if rubbed again and again by someone's thumb (clue 1: the child held this piece often). Quiet, dignified, grief without gore. Lying down he is a 28x22 px box (the standing king box 22x28 turned on its side), drawn on the 32x32 canvas of one cell.
groups.details_en: It must be the clear focal point of its room: the longest lying piece in the game (28 px against 22 for a pawn), with the cleanest silhouette on the board and the most empty floor around it. No face (a chess king has none). Treat with solemn respect. CELL FIT (owner decision 2026-10-12: a chess piece is smaller than its cell). The canvas is 32x32, exactly one cell. A piece lying on its side is its standing body box turned 90 degrees: the fallen King is at most 28x22 px. Outline included, it rests on the line y=30 and is centred on x=16, so at least 2 px of empty canvas remain on every side and nothing touches or crosses a canvas edge; a tilted or half-fallen piece keeps its whole silhouette inside x 2..29 and y 2..29.
groups.avoid_en: gore, blood, red, a face with mouth, a crown with jewels, blue, glow effects, other pieces
groups.palette_en: The worn patch of the base is a lighter, smoother ivory #F6EFDD.
groups.notes_vi: Vua trắng nằm nghiêng, tâm điểm cảm xúc của T1. Đáy đế mòn nhẵn một chỗ (manh mối 1: đứa trẻ đã cầm quân này rất nhiều). Nghiêm trang, không máu.

groups.subject_en: The four promotion tokens that the child's hand offers in the ending on the desk board (Queen, Rook, Bishop, Knight): shining new white pieces on little wooden discs. Bumping one plays a bittersweet epilogue and changes nothing on the board. They are kind and tempting, never a trap: the pawn's refusal must feel like a loving 'no'. Each piece is the polished, perfect counterpart of the scuffed survivors seen all game.
groups.details_en: Each image uses the SAME canvas size, the SAME base-centre anchor and the SAME palette. Four pieces in the same style so they read as one set. The bump frames keep the exact same drawing of the token as its resting pose with only the tilt and rocking changed. CELL FIT (owner decision 2026-10-12: a chess piece is smaller than its cell). The canvas is 32x32, exactly one cell: the whole token (piece plus disc) fits a 24x28 px box: the pale wooden disc is 24 px wide and 4 px tall, the queen piece standing on it is at most 20x24 px and the rook, bishop and knight pieces at most 18x20 px (a size smaller than on the board because they stand on a disc), centred on x=16, so at least 2 px of empty canvas remain on every side in every bump frame as well.
groups.avoid_en: gore, red, crayon blue, scuffs or cracks (these are perfect), faces, gold crowns, effect sprites
groups.palette_en: Disc wood #C9A878 with a thin golden-yellow rim #F2C23C (the interactable colour).
groups.notes_vi: Bốn quân phong cấp mới tinh đặt trên đĩa gỗ nhỏ: lời mời tử tế từ bàn tay đứa trẻ. Chạm vào thì chạy một câu kết, bàn cờ không đổi. Pawn từ chối bằng cách bước qua và đi ra khỏi mép bàn.

groups.title_vi: Ký ức các quân được cứu và nét sáp xanh cho quân chưa cứu (Act 6)
groups.anchor: base centre at (16,30): the base sits on the line y=30 with 2 px of empty canvas under it
groups.subject_en: The three Act-6 memory alcoves behind the lid: a soft memory figure of each rescued piece (Pebble 'Left is yours', Slant 'Right is yours', Stout 'Back is yours'). If a piece was NOT rescued the alcove shows a blue crayon outline of that piece instead ('drawn before you'), so nobody soft-locks and the child's help is still felt even though the child is cut off. (Folder ids are alcove_memory_<piece> so they never collide with the wall drawings memory_<piece> of the world lane.)
groups.details_en: Memories: soft translucent glow, no hard outline, no cartoon. Crayon outlines: thick wobbly wax-crayon line, paper texture showing through, one colour only. Each image uses the SAME canvas size, the SAME base-centre anchor and the SAME palette. CELL FIT (owner decision 2026-10-12: a chess piece is smaller than its cell). The canvas is 32x32, exactly one cell: each figure is the standing piece of its kind, a knight, bishop or rook of at most 20x24 px, centred on x=16 with its base on y=30, so at least 2 px of empty canvas remain on every side, shimmer and wobble frames included.
groups.avoid_en: near-black outlines on the memories, red, gore, faces, text, effect sprites
groups.palette_en: Memories: warm ivory #F1E8D2 at 60 percent opacity, soft pale outline #FFFFFF at 40 percent. Crayon outlines: crayon blue #3A6FE0 (the child's colour, allowed here because the child drew them).
groups.notes_vi: Ba hốc ký ức ở Act 6: bóng ký ức mờ của Pebble, Slant, Stout. Nếu chưa cứu quân nào thì chỗ đó là nét sáp xanh vẽ viền quân ấy. Đảm bảo không ai bị kẹt cốt truyện.

groups.title_vi: Vật cầm của Pawn: kiếm gỗ, bút chì, thước, cục tẩy
groups.anchor: grip pivot at (16,26), blade pointing north (the WeaponPivot rotates it); the whole weapon spans y=2..28 inside the cell
groups.subject_en: The weapons the white pawn holds on its WeaponPivot, one overlay per skill: Wooden Sword, Pencil Thrust, Ruler Blade (the alternate Strike, stored beside the Wooden Sword as a second weapon file) and the Eraser Guard plate. They are separate from the pawn body so the owner can redraw either independently.
groups.details_en: One weapon per file, drawn as a held overlay with the blade/tip pointing NORTH (up) on the canvas and the grip pivot at (16,26): the WeaponPivot node rotates the sprite, so draw it straight and rotation-ready with at least 2 px of empty margin all round. No hand, no wrist, no pawn body and no motion trail on the image (the swing arcs are separate effects). Right-handed grip side faces south. Same pixel scale, outline and light as the actors; the object is a toy or stationery item, never a real weapon. CELL FIT (owner decision 2026-10-12: a chess piece is smaller than its cell, and so is what it holds): the overlay is drawn on the 32x32 canvas of one cell, the whole weapon (tip to grip end) at most 26 px long and at most 8 px wide, standing from y=2 at the tip down to y=28 at the end of the grip, with the grip pivot at (16,26) and 2 px of empty canvas on every side.
groups.avoid_en: a hand or arm, motion blur, glow, text or ruler numerals (tick marks only), real-steel look, sharp realistic edges, red
groups.palette_en: Toy sword: tin-silver #B9C1CC / #8E97A3 / #646C78, leather #8A5A3A. Pencil: faded yellow #D8B23A, graphite #4A4A52, eraser pink #E8A0A8, ferrule #B8B8C0. Ruler: boxwood #E4C77A / #C9A24B, tick ink #2B2B2B. Eraser: pink #E8A0A8 / #C97B88 / #A85C68, sleeve cream #EFE3C0.
groups.notes_vi: Vật cầm riêng khỏi thân Pawn (WeaponPivot xoay). Vẽ thẳng, mũi hướng lên; mỗi kỹ năng một file.

groups.title_vi: Súng bắn bi (Marble Launcher, biến thể hoãn)
groups.anchor: base-bottom centre at (16,30): the base rim sits on the line y=30 (the lowest drawn body row is y=29) with 2 px of empty canvas under it; every chess piece stands on this one anchor, so a shorter piece just leaves more empty canvas above its head
groups.subject_en: Marble Launcher (deferred variant, extension recipe E7): a stationary ranged toy in the Black army: a squat charcoal-painted wooden barrel on a round chess-style pedestal, a brass spring plunger at the back and a clear glass marble resting in the muzzle, two small dull red eyes on the barrel's collar. It fires a marble along a row or column after a readable wind-up (the marble's lane is drawn as a rook-style telegraph). It never walks far: it pivots on its base. Quiet menace, a toy that shoots toys.
groups.details_en: Enemy clips are drawn in the FRONT view only; the game rotates or flips the sprite for other facings and the separate back-view and side-view body stills carry the facing. The attack clip never plays for enemies: intent is shown by windup, commit and recover. The piece is a toy gadget in the Black army, so its working parts may be part of the silhouette, but it still has no arms, no legs and no mouth. CELL FIT (owner decision 2026-10-12: a chess piece is smaller than its cell). The canvas is 32x32, exactly one cell. The standing rook body is at most 20x24 px, outline included, centred on x=16 with its base rim on y=30, so its top sits at y=6 and at least 2 px of empty canvas remain on every side: never exactly cell-sized, never taller than the cell, never touching or crossing a canvas edge. Relative heights follow a real chess set (pawn 22 px, knight, bishop and rook 24, queen 26, king 28; bosses on one cell are a little wider than their class and never beyond 24x28). In EVERY frame, squash, stretch, tilt, lean, lunge and lift included, every pixel of the piece stays inside x 2..29 and y 2..29: the headroom above the resting top is 4 px, a lift and a stretch together never use more than that, and a tilt or lean never pushes a side past x=2 or x=29; if a pose would not fit, shorten the stretch or the lift first and never the margin. The pixel measures written in the poses are already scaled to this body size.
groups.avoid_en: legs, mouths, weapons drawn as separate held objects, gore, blood, red anywhere except the dull seams and the commit flash, crayon blue, golden yellow, floor shadows, effect sprites
groups.palette_en: Shared palette of the style block.
groups.notes_vi: Biến thể hoãn (có thể bỏ). Bắn bi theo hàng hoặc cột; bị đánh bại thì thành đồ chơi bình thường.
groups.used_in: Not placed in the base; ready for the owner's extension recipe E7 (a Rook-style lane attack)

poses_en: Rest: Marble Launcher standing upright, base flat, eyes dull and watching. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
A slight 1 px sway to the left, the top 1 px lower. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
A slight 1 px sway to the right, 1 px taller, eyes blink as thin lines for this frame only. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Squash: the body compresses 2 px and leans 5 degrees toward the facing direction. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Hop lift: the base is 2 px off the floor, body stretched 1 px, leaning 8 degrees forward. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Peak: the base is 2 px up, the working parts one shade brighter. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Land: the base is flat, squash 2 px, the lean returns to upright. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Notice: the head swings toward the hero, the body rising 2 px, eyes sharp and red-orange. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.
Locked: steady, a 1 px lean toward the hero, seams dark orange. VIEW: front view, the piece faces the camera.

groups.title_vi: Búa lên dây cót (Wind-Up Hammer, biến thể hoãn)
groups.anchor: base-bottom centre at (16,30): the base rim sits on the line y=30 (the lowest drawn body row is y=29) with 2 px of empty canvas under it; every chess piece stands on this one anchor, so a shorter piece just leaves more empty canvas above its head
groups.subject_en: Wind-Up Hammer (deferred variant, extension recipe E7): a Black-army tin wind-up toy on a round chess-style pedestal: a squat charcoal-painted tin body with a big brass key turning in its back and one spring-loaded wooden mallet arm that slams the cell in front of it (a toy mechanism, not a limb). Two small dull red eyes on the tin collar. The key visibly winds up before the slam, so the tell is readable. A clockwork toy that hits hard and slowly.
groups.details_en: Enemy clips are drawn in the FRONT view only; the game rotates or flips the sprite for other facings and the separate back-view and side-view body stills carry the facing. The attack clip never plays for enemies: intent is shown by windup, commit and recover. The piece is a toy gadget in the Black army, so its working parts may be part of the silhouette, but it still has no arms, no legs and no mouth. CELL FIT (owner decision 2026-10-12: a chess piece is smaller than its cell). The canvas is 32x32, exactly one cell. The standing rook body is at most 20x24 px, outline included, centred on x=16 with its base rim on y=30, so its top sits at y=6 and at least 2 px of empty canvas remain on every side: never exactly cell-sized, never taller than the cell, never touching or crossing a canvas edge. Relative heights follow a real chess set (pawn 22 px, knight, bishop and rook 24, queen 26, king 28; bosses on one cell are a little wider than their class and never beyond 24x28). In EVERY frame, squash, stretch, tilt, lean, lunge and lift included, every pixel of the piece stays inside x 2..29 and y 2..29: the headroom above the resting top is 4 px, a lift and a stretch together never use more than that, and a tilt or lean never pushes a side past x=2 or x=29; if a pose would not fit, shorten the stretch or the lift first and never the margin. The pixel measures written in the poses are already scaled to this body size.
groups.avoid_en: legs, mouths, weapons drawn as separate held objects, gore, blood, red anywhere except the dull seams and the commit flash, crayon blue, golden yellow, floor shadows, effect sprites
groups.palette_en: Shared palette of the style block.
groups.notes_vi: Biến thể hoãn (có thể bỏ). Búa gỗ gắn lò xo đập ô phía trước sau khi lên dây cót.
groups.used_in: Not placed in the base; ready for the owner's extension recipe E7 (a one-cell melee hit with a long tell)
